# SDAIA Academy Course Catalog

> The SDAIA Academy course catalog: learning paths in AI Engineering and Data Science over shared Foundations, with a page for every course.

# USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- On the learning path: [Start here](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked 30-day follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/practice.html

## Description

The Academy's published four-day course plus a capstone day, delivered Arabic-first. Day one covers where AI helps and harms, safe use, and structured requests with persistent context. Day two applies them to Arabic and English writing, reading and extraction, spreadsheets and presentations. Day three covers deep research with verification, source-grounded notebooks, custom assistants and workflow redesign. Day four introduces agents with connectors and approvals, and building a small tool from a requirements document. In the capstone each participant redesigns one real recurring task and measures the gain over two trials against a baseline.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply a structured request pattern with persistent context to writing, summarising and extraction tasks in Arabic and English.
- Use an assistant to analyse a spreadsheet and produce a chart and a summary, with every reported figure checked by recalculation.
- Prepare a research brief with a deep-research tool and a source-grounded notebook, tracing each key claim to a source that exists and supports it.
- Configure a custom assistant with instructions, reference files and test questions for a recurring team task.
- Configure an agent run that uses a connector under least-privilege permissions with a human approval step, and identify the prompt-injection risk in its inputs.
- Draft a requirements document for a small internal tool and produce a working prototype with a generative coding platform, tested against three checks.
- Design an AI-assisted version of a real recurring task and measure the change in time and quality against a baseline over two trials.
- Prepare a personal adoption plan over one, seven and thirty days, including tasks kept AI-off to preserve skill and checks that stop unverified work reaching colleagues.

## Prerequisites

- Uses documents, email and spreadsheets in daily work
- Brings one real recurring task from their own job, described without confidential details

## Next courses

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: الأساس: أين يساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي وأين يضرّ

- أين يساعد وأين يضرّ
- التصنيف قبل المشاركة
- الطلب المهيكل
- الحوار والسياق الدائم

### Day 2: المهام اليومية

- الكتابة والمستوى اللغوي
- القراءة والاستخراج
- الجداول والتحقق من الأرقام
- العروض والصور

### Day 3: البحث والمعرفة الموثوقة

- البحث المعمق والتحقق
- الدفاتر المستندة إلى المصادر
- المساعدات المخصصة
- إعادة تصميم سير العمل

### Day 4: الوكلاء والأدوات الصغيرة والتبنّي المسؤول

- الوكلاء والموصِّلات
- من الفكرة إلى المتطلبات
- ابنِ واختبر وشارك
- التبنّي المسؤول

### Day 5: عروض المشروع الختامي


## Topics

### Foundations: where AI helps and where it harms

- Task-level evidence and the uneven frontier
- Delegation, description, discernment and diligence
- Classification before sharing
- Structured requests, dialogue and persistent context

### Everyday tasks

- Arabic and English writing, editing and register
- Reading, summarising and extraction
- Spreadsheets and data analysis
- Presentations and images

### Research and trustworthy knowledge

- Deep research and verification
- Source-grounded notebooks and projects
- Custom assistants and reusable skills
- Workflow redesign

### Agents and small tools

- Agents and scheduled tasks
- Connectors, permissions and prompt injection
- From idea to requirements document and agent instruction file
- Build, test and share a prototype; production deployment belongs to developers

### Responsible adoption

- The cost of unchecked output passed to colleagues
- Keeping your own skill: deliberate AI-off practice
- Disclosure and records
- The one, seven and thirty day plan

### Measuring value

- Baselines before change
- Time and quality measures
- Two trials and honest reporting
- Costs of checking and rework

# FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-101/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-101/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-101/practice.html

## Description

Participants write Python the way data and AI work needs it: small typed functions over collections and files, errors that fail loudly, and code moved out of notebooks into scripts that rerun. The case is a fictional regional water utility with synthetic meter readings in comma-separated values (CSV) files and bilingual service tickets in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Lines. Each day opens with an AI-off drill in reading, tracing or debugging code by hand, and the labs grow into a command-line tool that validates readings, flags anomalies and writes a summary report. Arabic text normalisation and SQL are left to FN-104, version control to FN-102.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain what a short program prints, step by step, including name binding, shared mutable lists and dictionaries, and scope.
- Distinguish when a notebook, a script or an importable module is the right home for a piece of code.
- Implement typed functions that load, validate and aggregate records with lists, dictionaries, sets and comprehensions.
- Apply exception handling and input validation so that each bad record is reported with a reason instead of crashing or passing silently.
- Use a repeatable debugging method: reproduce, shrink the input, form a hypothesis, test it, fix, and add a regression check.
- Prepare a command-line tool from an exploratory notebook, with an entry point, arguments and a written report.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-202.md)
- Has written and run a short program in any language, or completed the guided pre-work on values, conditions and loops

## Next courses

- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-204.md)
- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- [DS-202 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-202.md)
- [DS-203 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-203.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)
- [DS-206 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-206.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Read before you write

- Values, names and references
- Functions with clear contracts
- Type hints and a checker
- Parsons problems

### Day 2: Collections for data work

- Dictionaries for counting and grouping
- Sets and membership
- Comprehensions and generators
- Records as data classes

### Day 3: Files, text and failure

- CSV and JSON Lines
- Text, bytes and encodings
- Exceptions that explain
- A debugging method

### Day 4: From notebook to tool

- What notebooks hide
- Scripts, modules and an entry point
- Tests as a safety net
- Learning with an assistant without losing the skill

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Reading and tracing code

- Values, names and references
- Mutation and aliasing
- Scope and the call stack
- Predict-the-output and Parsons problems

### Functions and types

- Decomposing a task into small functions
- Type hints and a type checker
- Docstrings and doctests
- Modules and the standard library

### Collections for data

- Lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets
- Comprehensions and generators
- Sorting with keys, counting and grouping
- Data classes for records

### Files, text and errors

- CSV and JSON Lines
- Bytes, UTF-8 and decoding errors, with Arabic examples
- Exceptions that explain
- Reading tracebacks

### From notebook to tool

- Hidden state in notebooks
- Entry points and arguments
- Logging instead of print
- Assistants as tutors, not authors

# FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-102/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-102/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-102/practice.html

## Description

Participants take a working but fragile analysis project and make it something another person can rebuild, review and trust. The case is a fictional public library network whose monthly loans report sits in one folder with hard-coded paths, no history, unpinned packages and a key in a configuration file. Over three days they script the shell, put the project under version control, review and merge through pull requests, lock the environment, add tests that run on every push, and write a README that reports measured results. A peer then rebuilds it on a clean machine.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain what a commit, a branch, a merge and a pull request record, and how each can be undone safely.
- Identify where secrets, personal data, large outputs and machine-specific paths leak into a project.
- Use shell pipelines, redirection and exit codes to inspect and summarise files without writing a program.
- Use branches, pull requests and review comments to integrate a change, resolving a merge conflict without losing either side's work.
- Configure a project environment with declared dependencies and a lock file so that it installs identically on a clean machine.
- Implement tests that run in continuous integration and a README that reports measured results with the command that produced them.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- Opens a terminal and runs a Python script with arguments

## Next courses

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-204.md)
- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- [AE-306 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-306.md)
- [DS-311 · Data Quality, Labelling and Pipelines for Analysis](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-311.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Shell and history

- Working in the shell
- Pipelines over text
- First commits
- Reading and undoing history

### Day 2: Collaborate and lock

- Branches and pull requests
- Merge conflicts
- Environments and lock files
- Secrets and large files

### Day 3: Test, automate, report

- Tests for calculations
- Continuous integration
- A README that reports results
- Reproduction from a README

### Day 4: Capstone: a reproducible repository and its defence


## Topics

### The shell

- Paths, permissions and environment variables
- Pipes, redirection and filters
- Exit codes and short scripts
- Remote login with secure shell (SSH) keys

### Version control and review

- Commits, staging and history
- Branches, merges and conflicts
- Pull requests and review etiquette
- Undoing mistakes without rewriting shared history

### Reproducible environments

- Virtual environments
- Declared dependencies and lock files
- Pinned interpreter versions
- Data and outputs kept outside the code

### Tests and continuous integration

- Unit tests for calculations
- Small synthetic test data
- A pipeline that runs on every push

### Hygiene and reporting

- Secrets out of history: rotate, then clean
- Ignore files and pre-commit hooks
- A README that reports results
- A change log and a tagged release

# FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-103/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-103/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-103/practice.html

## Description

Participants learn the minimum mathematics both badges assume and compute every idea twice: by hand on a small case and in array code. The case is a fictional desalination plant with synthetic pump and sensor readings. Vectors and matrices describe the readings and their similarity; least squares and principal components find structure; derivatives, the chain rule and gradient descent fit an energy curve; conditional probability, distributions and seeded simulation explain alarm rates and the uncertainty of an estimate. The capstone ties the three strands into one short analysis.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain dot products, norms, matrix products and rank as operations on data, and predict the shape of each result.
- Compute cosine similarity, a least-squares fit and principal components with array code, checking each against a hand calculation.
- Describe derivatives, gradients and the chain rule on a computational graph, and trace one backward pass by hand.
- Implement gradient descent for a small model and identify step-size problems from the loss curve.
- Compute the probability that an alarm signals a real fault with Bayes rule, and confirm it by seeded simulation.
- Use simulation to estimate an expectation and its Monte Carlo error, and show how the error shrinks with sample size.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- Solves a linear equation and reads a function graph at secondary-school level

## Next courses

- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Data as vectors

- Vectors and similarity
- Matrices as transformations
- Loops versus vectorised code
- Rank and redundant sensors

### Day 2: Structure and fit

- Projection and least squares
- When least squares misbehaves
- Covariance and principal components
- Language models use the same algebra

### Day 3: Gradients

- Derivatives as local slopes
- The chain rule on a graph
- Gradient descent
- Penalties and their effect

### Day 4: Probability and simulation

- Conditional probability and base rates
- Distributions for counts and measurements
- Expectation and Monte Carlo error
- Probability inside models

### Day 5: Capstone: a second plant and the oral check


## Topics

### Vectors and matrices as data

- Dot products, norms and cosine similarity
- Matrix products as transformations
- Shapes, broadcasting and vectorised code
- Rank and linear independence

### Structure in data

- Projection and least squares
- Covariance and principal component analysis (PCA)
- Eigenvectors and singular values in brief
- Floating-point limits and conditioning

### Change and optimisation

- Derivatives and partial derivatives
- Gradients and the chain rule on a graph
- Automatic differentiation as the chain rule in code
- Gradient descent and step size
- Convexity, local minima and penalties

### Probability

- Conditional probability and Bayes rule
- Binomial, Poisson, normal and categorical distributions
- Expectation, variance and covariance
- Likelihood and cross-entropy as training losses

### Simulation

- Seeds and pseudo-random generators
- Monte Carlo estimates and their error
- Law of large numbers and the central limit theorem

# FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-104/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-104/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-104/practice.html

## Description

Participants answer questions from data and show the answers are right. The case is a fictional courier company with synthetic shipments, hubs, couriers and delivery attempts. In an embedded analytical database they write joins, grouping and window functions, predicting each result first and catching fan-out and NULL errors. In a dataframe library they type, clean, reshape and join raw exports. At the boundary they handle delimited, JSON and columnar files, legacy Arabic encodings, Hijri and Gregorian dates, time zones, and schema checks that stop a bad batch.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify the grain and keys of each table and predict the row count of a join before running it.
- Implement SQL queries with joins, grouping, common table expressions and window functions that answer operational questions.
- Prepare an analysis-ready table from raw exports with a dataframe library, handling types, missing values, duplicates, dates and reshaping.
- Apply Arabic text normalisation and encoding repair so that names and addresses match across sources.
- Configure schema and quality checks that reject or quarantine a bad batch with a reason.
- Compare delimited, JSON Lines and columnar formats by size, read speed, types preserved and fitness for exchange.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- Writes Python functions that read files and loop over records

## Next courses

- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [AE-306 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-306.md)
- [DS-202 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-202.md)
- [DS-203 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-203.md)
- [DS-206 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-206.md)
- [DS-307 · Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-307.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Query with care

- Grain, keys and cardinality
- Filters and NULL
- Joins that do not double count
- Grouping and common table expressions

### Day 2: Windows and checks

- Ranking and top-N
- Change over time
- Sequences of events
- Testing queries

### Day 3: Wrangle with dataframes

- Loading and typing
- Missing values and duplicates
- Reshape and join
- Same result, two engines

### Day 4: Formats, text and validation

- Choosing a file format
- Encodings and Arabic text
- Dates and time zones
- Checks that stop a bad batch

### Day 5: Capstone: the operations brief and its live rerun


## Topics

### Relational querying

- Tables, keys, grain and cardinality
- Filters, NULL and three-valued logic
- Joins, fan-out and anti joins
- Grouping and common table expressions

### Window functions

- Partitions and ordering
- Ranking, lag and lead
- Running and moving aggregates
- Testing a query against known answers

### Dataframes

- Typed loading and nullable types
- Missing values and duplicates
- Tidy data: melt and pivot
- Joins with validated cardinality
- Eager and lazy engines

### Text, dates and encodings

- UTF-8 and legacy Arabic code pages
- Arabic letter variants, diacritics, elongation and digits
- Hijri and Gregorian dates
- Time zones and offsets

### Formats and validation

- Delimited, JSON Lines and columnar files
- Declared schemas and range checks
- Rejecting a load versus quarantining rows
- Data dictionaries and cleaning logs

# FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-105/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-105/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-105/practice.html

## Description

Participants find out how models are made and where they fail by doing the work in small steps. The case is the after-sales service of a fictional home-appliance retailer. They fit a nearest-neighbour rule and a line by hand, then train and validate a classifier that predicts which repair tickets need a second visit, overfit it on purpose and find planted leakage. They then count tokens in Arabic and English, sample from a small open-weight model, test recall across a long warranty document, and check a published model claim against its evidence.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how a supervised model fits labelled examples by reducing a loss, and why its score on training data overstates its score on new data.
- Use a train, validation and test split and cross-validation to compare a baseline with two models.
- Analyse a pipeline for target, duplicate and temporal leakage and measure the score before and after each fix.
- Compute precision, recall and the cost of errors at several thresholds and choose one for a stated cost.
- Describe how a language model splits text into tokens, predicts and samples the next token, and uses its context window.
- Identify the limits of a model claim, including fabrication, knowledge cut-off, benchmark contamination and partial versus complete credit.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- Loads a table into a dataframe and computes a proportion

## Next courses

- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Models from examples

- Learning by hand
- Training and testing
- Overfitting on purpose
- Thresholds and the cost of errors

### Day 2: Evaluation and leakage

- Cross-validation
- Finding leakage
- Error by subgroup
- Tokens and next-token prediction

### Day 3: Language models and their limits

- Sampling and variability
- Context and recall
- Fabrication and grounding
- Reading AI evidence

### Day 4: Capstone: the modelling report and its defence


## Topics

### Learning from examples

- Features, labels and loss
- Nearest neighbours and linear models by hand
- Trees and small neural networks in brief

### Generalisation and evaluation

- Train, validation and test sets
- Overfitting and learning curves
- Cross-validation
- Confusion matrix, precision, recall and thresholds

### Leakage and data

- Target, duplicate and temporal leakage
- Pipelines fitted on training data only
- Distribution shift and subgroup error

### How language models work

- Tokens and Arabic script
- Next-token probabilities and sampling
- Pretraining and post-training
- Context windows, tools and retrieval in brief

### Limits and evidence

- Fabrication and sycophancy
- Knowledge cut-off and model cards
- Benchmarks, contamination and harness effects
- Partial credit against completed tasks

# FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Shared Foundations: the entry courses for both badge tracks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FN-100.md)
- On the learning path: [Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-106/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-106/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/fn-106/practice.html

## Description

Participants make one small build lawful and responsible: a parent-enquiry assistant for a fictional private school group that drafts replies from attendance and fee records with a language model. They map its personal data and minimise it under the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), classify each data set under the National Data Management Office (NDMO) policy, decide what may reach an external model, turn the SDAIA AI Ethics Principles into tests, assess risk with the National AI Risk Management Framework, and write the disclosure and records the build needs.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the PDPL obligations that govern a build, from lawful basis and minimisation to rights, retention, transfer and breach handling.
- Distinguish what the data classification, data sharing and open data policies and the SDAIA Generative AI Guidelines each decide.
- Classify each data set of the build under the four NDMO classification levels and derive the rule for sending it to an external model service.
- Apply minimisation and pseudonymisation to the data the assistant sends, and test whether records can be re-identified.
- Prepare a risk assessment that places the assistant in an ethics risk tier and works through the four phases of the national risk framework.
- Test the assistant against the ethics principles for fairness across Arabic and English enquiries, transparency and human review, and draft the disclosure parents see.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- Reads a short Python program that calls a web API

## Next courses

- [AE-207 · Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-207.md)
- [DS-202 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-202.md)
- [DS-206 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-206.md)
- [DS-207 · Responsible Data Practice and Conduct in Analytical Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-207.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Personal data and the law

- Where personal data flows in a build
- Lawful basis and minimisation
- Pseudonymisation and its limits
- Rights, retention and breaches

### Day 2: Classify, share and send

- Data classification levels
- What may reach an external model
- Sharing with another entity
- Licences and provenance

### Day 3: Ethics and risk in practice

- Principles into tests
- Testing the assistant

### Day 4: Capstone: the responsible build pack

### Personal data in a build

- Personal data in prompts, logs and stores
- Lawful basis, purpose and minimisation

- Handling rules for external services

# AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and evaluate a tabular prediction model the way an engineer would ship it. On synthetic appointment data from a fictional clinic network they frame the prediction, prepare features inside a pipeline, set a baseline, move to regularised linear models and boosted trees, choose a validation scheme that matches time and patient grouping, find and remove planted leakage, pick metrics and a threshold from the cost of each error, analyse errors by slice, and compare two models with an interval rather than a single score. Every result is reproduced from a script with a fixed seed.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish random, grouped and time-ordered validation and state which one each described prediction task requires.
- Prepare a feature pipeline that imputes, encodes and scales inside cross-validation so that no statistic is computed on held-out rows.
- Implement a baseline, a regularised linear model and a gradient-boosted tree model and score each on the same validation splits.
- Analyse a dataset for target leakage and train-test contamination and remove each problem found.
- Compute ranking, threshold and calibration metrics and choose an operating threshold from a stated cost of each error type.
- Analyse errors by subgroup and slice to find where the model fails, then test one data or feature change aimed at the worst slice.
- Evaluate whether a challenger model beats the baseline using a paired comparison with a confidence interval and a stated minimum effect.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- Writes Python functions and uses dataframes to filter, join and group a table
- Computes a mean, a variance and a conditional probability by hand

## Next courses

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Frame and prepare

- A prediction is a decision at a moment
- Baselines before models
- Features in a pipeline
- Time, lags and history

### Day 2: Models and validation

- Linear models and regularisation
- Trees and boosting
- The validation scheme decides the score
- Hunting leakage

### Day 3: Metrics and errors

- Metrics that match the decision
- Calibration and thresholds
- Error analysis by slice
- Fixing one failure

### Day 4: Compare and report

- Is the challenger better
- Searching without fooling yourself
- Regression in the same frame
- Reproducible results and a model card

### Day 5: Capstone: a prediction project and its defence


## Topics

### Framing a prediction task

- Target, unit and moment of prediction
- The decision the prediction serves
- Cost of each error type
- Rule-based and majority baselines

### Data preparation and features

- Missing values and imputation
- Encoding categories
- Scaling
- Date, lag and history features
- Pipelines that fit only on training folds
- Data checks before training

### Model families

- Linear and logistic regression with regularisation
- Decision trees
- Bagging and random forests
- Gradient boosting
- Bias and variance
- Hyperparameter search
- Feature importance and its limits

### Validation and leakage

- Holdout and k-fold
- Grouped and time-ordered splits
- Nested search
- Kinds of leakage
- Keeping a test set untouched

### Metrics and thresholds

- Confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1
- ROC and precision-recall curves
- Class imbalance and class weights
- Calibration
- Cost-based thresholds
- Regression metrics

### Error analysis and comparison

- Slicing and subgroup error
- Bootstrap intervals
- Paired comparison of models
- Minimum effect of interest
- Multiple comparisons

### Reproducible results

- Seeds and locked environments
- Re-running from a clean clone
- A model card stub

# AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/practice.html

## Description

Participants go from tensors to a working generative model and learn what each layer of the stack does. For a fictional crafts cooperative they write a training loop by hand, debug a network that will not learn, adapt a pretrained image model to synthetic textile images, implement attention for a toy sequence, build bilingual semantic search with sentence embeddings, and generate text with a small open-weight model while varying sampling settings. They finish by comparing model families on quality, size, latency, licence and cost for three of the cooperative's use cases.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how a transformer turns input tokens into next-token probabilities, naming the role of embeddings, attention, the context window and sampling.
- Implement a training loop with a loss, an optimiser, mini-batches and validation checks, and use it to train a small network.
- Apply a debugging checklist to a network whose loss does not fall and correct each fault found.
- Use transfer learning to adapt a pretrained image model to a new label set with little data, and measure the improvement over training from scratch.
- Use sentence embeddings to build and test a bilingual semantic search over product descriptions.
- Measure how temperature, nucleus sampling and the instruction change the outputs of a small open-weight language model.
- Evaluate model families for three stated use cases on quality, size, latency, licence terms and cost, and recommend one per use case.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- Multiplies matrices and computes a derivative with the chain rule
- Has trained and evaluated a model with a train, validation and test split

## Next courses

- [AE-206 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-206.md)
- [AE-301 · Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-301.md)
- [AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-304.md)
- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Tensors and training

- Tensors, shapes and gradients
- Writing the training loop
- Learning rates, batches and regularisation
- When training goes wrong

### Day 2: Vision and transfer

- Convolutions and what they detect
- Pretrained backbones
- Fine-tuning with little data
- Evaluating a deep model

### Day 3: Transformers and embeddings

- Tokens, including Arabic
- Attention step by step
- Sentence embeddings
- Multilingual search and its failures

### Day 4: Generation and model choice

- Next-token prediction and sampling
- From base models to assistants
- Limits: fabrication, cut-off and context
- Choosing a model family

### Day 5: Capstone: a small model for the cooperative, defended live


## Topics

### Tensors and automatic differentiation

- Tensors, shapes and broadcasting
- Computational graphs and gradients
- Devices and number formats

### Training neural networks

- Losses and optimisers
- Mini-batches and learning rates
- Dropout, weight decay and augmentation
- Learning curves and early stopping
- Debugging training

### Convolutional networks and transfer learning

- Convolutions and pooling
- Pretrained backbones
- Freezing and fine-tuning
- Evaluating a deep model and checking for near-duplicates

### Sequence models and transformers

- Tokenisation, including Arabic
- Embeddings and position
- Self-attention
- Encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder models

### Embeddings and search

- Sentence embeddings
- Similarity measures
- Multilingual embeddings
- Recall at k

### How generation works

- Next-token prediction
- Greedy decoding, temperature and nucleus sampling
- Context windows
- Instruction and preference tuning at concept level
- Reasoning effort and its cost
- Fabricated answers and knowledge cut-off

### Model families and choice

- Encoders, decoders, diffusion and vision-language models
- Open-weight versus hosted models
- Size, latency and cost
- Licences and data provenance

# AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/practice.html

## Description

Participants build a bilingual rider assistant for a fictional transit authority on top of any language model, hosted or open-weight. They call models through a provider-neutral interface, extract validated structured data from rider messages, add tool calls to a synthetic trip-status service, ground answers in a policy corpus with citations and abstention, write a small evaluation set and run the assistant against it, and add input and output checks for personal data and instruction-like text. The result is a small tested web service.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare the main model API shapes and identify what changes in code when an application switches provider or moves to a local model.
- Implement structured extraction from free-text messages with schema validation, bounded retries and a fallback path.
- Implement tool calling for two services with typed arguments, argument validation and handling of tool errors.
- Implement a grounded answering step that retrieves policy passages, cites them and declines when the corpus holds no answer.
- Prepare a small evaluation set and measure the assistant with code-based checks and one model-graded check validated against labels.
- Configure input and output checks for personal data, off-topic requests and instruction-like text inside retrieved content.
- Build a bilingual assistant service that combines structured extraction, tool calls and grounded answers behind a tested API.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- Calls a web API from Python and handles JSON
- Writes and runs unit tests

- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- [AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-304.md)
- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)
- [AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-311.md)
- [AE-312 · AI Cost Engineering and Model Routing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-312.md)

## Format and days

# AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and change software by directing coding agents while staying accountable for every merged line. On the booking-service repository of a fictional government digital-services unit, they read and debug code by hand, write a specification and a plan before delegating, make the repository agent-ready with a short context file, a skill and test commands, run an agent with scoped permissions in an isolated worktree, review its changes by risk, add property-based and mutation tests, scan generated code and dependencies for vulnerabilities, and gate everything in continuous integration. One assessed checkpoint is done without AI.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse an unfamiliar code base by hand to trace a request path and locate the cause of a failing test.
- Draft a specification with acceptance criteria and a plan of small, verifiable steps before delegating work to an agent.
- Configure a repository for agent work with a short context file, one reusable skill, scoped permissions and commands for tests and linting.
- Test agent-written code with unit, property-based and mutation tests and report what the original tests missed.
- Apply a risk-based review checklist to agent pull requests, including security scanning of the change and its dependencies.
- Configure continuous integration that runs tests, type checks, security scans and a dependency audit on every change.
- Deliver a feature through the specify, plan, execute and verify cycle with an agent and defend each design decision to a reviewer.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)

# AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/practice.html

## Description

Participants take two trained models from a notebook to a monitored service. For a fictional mutual insurer they package a claims-triage classifier and a similar-claims embedding model with pinned dependencies, register model versions, serve them behind a versioned API with input validation, build and scan a container image, run it on a single-node local cluster with health checks, add metrics, structured logs and traces, load-test and size the service, release a new version by canary and roll it back, and detect drift in a replayed stream of claims.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the path from a trained model to a served prediction, naming the artefact, image, registry, runtime, endpoint and monitor at each step.
- Prepare a model artefact with pinned dependencies, a version, an input and output signature and a reproducible build.
- Implement a versioned prediction API with input validation, typed errors and separate health and readiness checks.
- Configure a container image for the service, scan it for vulnerabilities and run it with resource limits on a single-node cluster.
- Implement metrics, structured logs and traces for the service and a dashboard for latency percentiles, error rate and prediction distribution.
- Measure latency and throughput under load and size workers and replicas to meet a latency objective at the lowest cost.
- Deliver a new model version by canary release, decide on promotion or rollback from monitored metrics and detect drift in replayed traffic.

# AE-206 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)

- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-206/practice.html

## Description

Participants find out where time and memory go between raw data and a served prediction, and fix the largest cost first. For a fictional agritech company they profile a data pipeline and a training step, estimate memory from weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache, apply mixed precision, batching, quantisation and pruning, export a model to a portable runtime, and benchmark latency, throughput and quality with repeated runs and intervals. Labs run on a laptop CPU, with an optional free notebook GPU, and every speed-up must be measured and checked for loss of quality.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how compute, memory capacity and memory bandwidth limit training and inference, and identify which one binds for a described workload.
- Measure where time goes in a data pipeline and a training step with profilers and timers, and remove the largest bottleneck.
- Compute the memory needed for weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache and check each estimate against measured peak memory.
- Apply mixed precision, batching and compilation and report their effect on speed, memory and accuracy.
- Apply post-training quantisation and pruning, export the model to a portable runtime and compare size, latency and quality with the original.
- Prepare a benchmark that controls warm-up, repetitions, batch size and input mix, and report percentiles with confidence intervals.
- Optimise a model and its serving path to meet a stated latency and memory budget on a target device while keeping quality within an agreed tolerance.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
- Reads a histogram and computes a percentile

## Next courses

- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Measure first

- Compute, memory and bandwidth
- Timers, profilers and noise
- Profiling a training step
- Fixing an input-bound pipeline

### Day 2: Memory and training efficiency

- Where memory goes
- Mixed precision
- Accumulation and checkpointing
- Compilation and fusion

### Day 3: Inference and compression

- Latency, throughput and batching
- Language model inference on a laptop
- Quantisation
- Pruning or a smaller model

### Day 4: Export and benchmark

- Export to a portable runtime
- A benchmark you can trust
- Quality must survive
- Budgets and trade-offs

### Day 5: Capstone: an optimisation study and its defence


## Topics

### The physics of a machine

- Compute, memory capacity and bandwidth
- The roofline idea
- Caches and data movement
- CPUs, GPUs and neural accelerators

### Measuring first

- Timers and profilers
- Warm-up and variance
- Percentiles
- Flame graphs
- Memory profiling

### Data pipelines

- File formats and decoding
- Parallel loading and prefetching
- Caching preprocessed data
- Input-bound versus compute-bound

### Training efficiently

- Batch size and throughput
- Mixed precision
- Gradient accumulation
- Activation checkpointing
- Compilation and operator fusion

### Inference

- Latency versus throughput
- Batching
- Key-value cache for language models
- Prefill and decode
- Time to first token and tokens per second

### Compression

- Quantisation formats
- Post-training versus quantisation-aware training
- Pruning
- Distillation at concept level
- Re-evaluating quality after compression

### Portable runtimes and export

- Exchange formats
- Graph optimisation
- Runtimes for CPUs and edge devices
- Runtimes for small language models

### Benchmarking

- Benchmark design
- Repeated runs and intervals
- Goodput against a service objective
- Energy per prediction as an estimate

# AE-207 · Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/practice.html

## Description

Participants turn data protection, security and responsible-AI duties into engineering work on one application. For a fictional housing support fund that uses a language model to summarise applicant documents and an eligibility screening model, they convert Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) obligations into testable requirements, classify every data flow, add masking, pseudonymisation and retention controls, test the assistant against prepared injection and leakage attacks, add basic controls, check the screening model for subgroup errors, record risks in a register using the national framework, and write a system card and a plain-language statement of limits for case officers and applicants. Full attack and hardening work is left to AE-308.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how PDPL principles, data classification levels and the AI Ethics Principles apply at each stage of a language model application.
- Classify the data flows of an AI application and implement the minimisation, masking and retention controls that follow from the classification.
- Test a language model application against prepared injection and data-leakage cases mapped to a standard risk list, and record which succeed.
- Implement basic controls: separation of untrusted content, output validation, least-privilege tool access and a human approval step for decisions about people.
- Analyse risks including subgroup errors of the screening model and third-party model terms, and record each in a risk register with likelihood, impact, treatment and owner.
- Defend the release conditions of an AI application to non-technical stakeholders using a system card, the risk register and a plain-language statement of limits.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Has built, or can read, a small language model application with retrieval
- Can name the four national data classification levels
- Computes error rates from a confusion matrix, as taught in FN-105 or AE-201

## Next courses

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Data duties in a build

- From law to engineering requirements
- Classify before you build
- Minimise, mask and pseudonymise
- Records, retention and deletion

### Day 2: Risks of language model applications

- A risk list for language model applications
- Prompt injection and data leakage
- Basic controls
- Risk assessment with the national framework

### Day 3: Fairness, documentation and stakeholders

- Fairness checks on the screening model
- Third-party models and licences
- System cards
- Communicating limits to stakeholders

### Day 4: Capstone: the responsible-use and security pack


## Topics

### From law and policy to requirements

- Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) principles for builders
- Lawful basis, purpose and minimisation
- Retention, deletion and data subject rights
- Transfers outside the Kingdom
- Records of processing
- Breach handling and notification duties

### Classification in a build

- The four national classification levels
- Classifying data flows
- What may reach a hosted model
- Masking and pseudonymisation

### Risks of language model applications

- The Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 for LLM Applications
- Prompt injection and data leakage
- Excessive agency and insecure tool use
- Insecure output handling
- The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications at concept level

### Basic controls

- Separating untrusted content
- Output validation
- Least-privilege tools
- Human approval for decisions about people
- Logging for audit without personal data

### Fairness and risk management

- Subgroup error rates
- Bias categories from the national bias guide
- Risk tiers in the AI Ethics Principles

- Build or buy notes

# AE-301 · Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/practice.html

## Description

Participants build the language layer of a customer-service system for a fictional regional water utility whose messages arrive in Modern Standard Arabic, Gulf dialect, Arabic written in Latin script and English. They trace text through tokenisers, embeddings and attention, build semantic search, route messages and extract account fields three ways (a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder), adapt a model with low-rank adapters in free notebook memory, and ship the chosen model as a small service with a model card. Every choice rests on scores by dialect, latency and cost.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how tokenisation, embeddings and attention turn Arabic and English text into model inputs, and where script, diacritics and dialect break that pipeline.
- Implement semantic search over a bilingual message archive and measure it for each language variety.
- Implement schema-validated extraction of account numbers, districts and complaint types from free text, masking personal fields before text reaches a hosted model.
- Apply low-rank adapter fine-tuning to an encoder within a fixed memory budget and compare it with full fine-tuning.
- Decide among a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder for message routing.
- Deliver the chosen model as a tested service with a model card that states its limits by language variety.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
- Computes precision, recall and F1 from predictions
- Reads and writes UTF-8 Arabic text in Python

## Next courses

- [AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-408.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Represent

- Tokenisation
- Embeddings and semantic search
- Inside the transformer
- Decision models

### Day 2: Generate

- Generative language models
- Prompting and structured outputs
- Retrieval-augmented generation
- Model selection and evaluation

### Day 3: Adapt

- Fine-tuning data
- Fine-tuning an encoder
- Low-rank and quantised adapters
- Evaluate and deploy

### Day 4: Capstone: a routing and extraction service and its defence


## Topics

### Representing text

- Subword tokenisers and token cost per language
- Normalising alef, hamza, ta marbuta and diacritics
- Dialect and Arabic in Latin script
- Embeddings and vector indexes

### Models for decisions

- Attention, encoders and decoders
- Baselines first
- Classification and token-classification heads
- A prompted model as a zero-shot classifier

### Generation in applications

- Sampling and consistency
- Structured outputs with validation
- Grounding in a rule corpus (depth in AE-304)
- Choosing by quality, latency, cost and licence

### Adapting and shipping

- Splits without leakage
- Full fine-tuning against low-rank and quantised adapters
- CPU latency, a small API and a demo
- Model cards with subgroup results

# AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/practice.html

## Description

Participants build an agent as a model in a loop calling typed tools inside a sandbox, with most of the engineering in the harness. For a fictional ports authority they write the loop from scratch, budget the context, add a context file, a skill and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, compare an agent SDK with their own harness, gate bookings in a checkpointed state graph, and ship a traced, evaluated and contained agent behind an API.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement a tool-calling agent loop without a framework, with typed tool schemas, a step budget and explicit completion criteria.
- Apply compaction, offloading of tool results and staged loading of skills, and measure the effect on tokens and success.
- Implement a protocol server over a document store and connect the agent to it through capability discovery.
- Design a checkpointed state-graph agent with a human approval gate at a defined risk threshold.
- Evaluate the agent over repeated trials, including runs against a seeded prompt injection.
- Deliver the agent as a traced API service gated by a smoke evaluation in continuous integration.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Writes typed Python and calls a web API that returns JSON
- Runs a container and reads its logs

## Next courses

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: From Model to Agent

- Three API shapes
- Structured outputs
- Tools
- The agent loop from scratch

### Day 2: Context Engineering

- Context as a budget
- Retrieval for agents
- Memory, skills and context files
- Model Context Protocol

### Day 3: Harness and Loop

- Anatomy of a harness
- Agent SDKs and hosted agents
- Loop engineering
- Evaluating agents

### Day 4: Graph and Production

- State graphs with checkpoints
- Several agents and agent-to-agent delegation
- Securing agents
- Production

### Day 5: Capstone: a research agent and its defence


## Topics

### From model to agent

- Typed tool schemas and useful tool errors
- The loop written from scratch
- Completion criteria and step budgets

### Context and protocols

- Context as a budget
- Compaction, offloading and cache-aware layout
- Context files, skills and memory files
- Model Context Protocol, current revision; agent-to-agent delegation as a concept

### Harness and loop

- Tools, context, state and feedback as the harness
- Agent SDKs against an own loop
- Verification inside the loop

### Graphs and several agents

- Checkpoints and interrupts
- Approval at risk thresholds, and approval prompts nobody reads
- When several agents pay

### Securing and shipping

- The agentic risk list of the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP)
- Private data, untrusted content, exit path: remove one leg
- Sandboxes and egress allowlists

# AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/practice.html

## Description

Participants treat evaluation as the specification of a language model application. Working on one synthetic case, a bilingual service assistant for a fictional licensing office, they read traces, name the failure modes, turn them into code-based checks and calibrated model-graded checks, evaluate an agent over repeated trials, compare two configurations with a sound statistical test, and wire the suite into a regression gate. Every number a participant reports comes from a run they executed.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish code-based checks, model-graded checks and human review, and state when each is the cheapest reliable instrument.
- Carry out open and axial coding of traces to produce a failure taxonomy with counts.
- Implement code-based evaluators for structure, grounding and policy rules.
- Calibrate a model-graded evaluator against human labels and report its agreement with an interval.
- Evaluate an agent on multi-step tasks for outcome and consistency over repeated trials.
- Decide between two configurations using a paired comparison with its uncertainty, cost and latency.
- Build a regression gate that blocks a change when a critical failure mode gets worse.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Reads a confusion matrix and computes precision and recall
- Has run a test suite in continuous integration

## Next courses

- [AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-405.md)
- [AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-406.md)
- [AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-407.md)
- [AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-408.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: See the failures

- Evaluation is the specification
- Traces are the raw material
- Open coding
- From codes to a failure taxonomy

### Day 2: Build the instruments

- Checks you can write in code
- Grounding and citation checks
- Model graders with binary criteria
- Calibrating a grader against people

### Day 3: Agents and comparisons

- Grading a transcript and an outcome
- Consistency over repeated trials
- Is B better than A
- Cost and latency belong in the decision

### Day 4: Gate the release

- Golden sets, versions and leakage
- A regression gate in continuous integration
- From offline suites to online monitoring
- Reporting results people can act on

### Day 5: Capstone: an evaluation suite and its release gate


## Topics

### Evaluation as specification

- Non-determinism and the gap between intent and behaviour
- Benchmarks versus application evaluations
- What a leaderboard does not tell you

### Error analysis

- Sampling traces
- Open and axial coding
- Failure taxonomies and saturation
- Prioritising by frequency and severity

### Evaluators

- Assertions and reference-based checks
- Binary criteria for model graders
- Calibration against human labels
- Correcting pass rates for grader error

### Agents and retrieval

- Grading transcript and outcome
- Consistency over repeated trials
- Groundedness and citation checks
- Arabic test sets

### Comparing and deciding

- Paired comparisons and bootstrap intervals
- Sample size and minimum effect
- Cost, latency and quality as one decision

### Evaluation in delivery

- Golden sets and leakage
- Regression gates
- Online monitoring and review queues
- Privacy of traces

# AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and measure the retrieval layer of a language model system for a fictional university: bilingual regulations, study plans with tables, scanned Arabic circulars and an enrolment statistics warehouse. Starting from a graded test set, they build lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation, parse and chunk documents by structure, filter by date and role, give an agent search tools and a small knowledge graph, and answer statistical questions through a semantic layer instead of free text-to-SQL.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a retrieval test set with graded relevance judgements and compute standard ranking metrics for each language.
- Implement lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation and compare them on quality and latency.
- Analyse parsing and chunking choices by scoring two parsers and two chunking schemes.
- Build retrieval that never returns a document the requester may not see or a superseded rule.
- Design an agentic search component that chooses among search tools and a small knowledge graph within a context budget.
- Evaluate free text-to-SQL against a semantic layer with validated SQL and decide which to ship.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Writes SQL joins and aggregations
- Computes precision and recall
- Has built a small grounded application with citations

## Format and days

### Day 1: Measure and search

- Retrieval is measured on its own
- Lexical search and Arabic text
- Dense retrieval and embedding choice
- Hybrid search and reranking

### Day 2: Prepare the corpus

- Parsing is a separate problem
- Chunking by structure
- Dates, versions and duplicates
- Permissions in the index

### Day 3: Agentic search and knowledge

- Search as tools for an agent
- Multi-step questions
- Paging and offloading
- Knowledge graphs for linked facts

### Day 4: Structured data and diagnosis

- Questions over a warehouse
- Semantic layers and validated SQL
- Cost, latency and freshness
- Diagnosing failures by component

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Measuring retrieval

- Graded relevance and pooling
- Recall at k, reciprocal rank and discounted gain
- Slicing by language and query type

### Search methods

- Inverted indexes and BM25
- Arabic normalisation and light stemming
- Multilingual embeddings and approximate nearest-neighbour indexes
- Rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking

### Preparing a corpus

- Parsing right-to-left text and tables
- Small specialised parsing models against general vision models
- Chunking by structure
- Effective dates and deduplication

### Agentic search and knowledge

- The cheapest tool that works first
- Iterative search and query decomposition
- Paging and offloading large results
- Knowledge graphs for multi-hop questions

### Structured data, access and trust

- Schema grounding and semantic layers
- Validating generated SQL
- Permission filters before ranking
- Retrieved text as untrusted input

# AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/practice.html

## Description

Participants run three systems of a fictional electricity distribution company in production: a fault-risk classifier retrained on monthly batches with planted drift, a field-crew assistant with retrieval and two tools, and an outage-ticket agent. They version everything that changes behaviour as one release unit, build pipelines with validation and promotion gates, release through canary stages with automatic rollback, trace requests, monitor drift and online quality, and keep the agent alive through crashes and runaway loops. Evaluators come ready-made from AE-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a release manifest that versions data, code, configuration, model, prompt, retrieval index and tool schemas as one unit.
- Build a retraining pipeline, started by a drift or schedule trigger, with data validation and a promotion gate that compares challenger and champion overall and by region.
- Deliver language model changes through an evaluation gate and a canary stage with an automatic rollback trigger.
- Configure request tracing, drift monitors and online evaluation with a review queue, and tune alert thresholds.
- Diagnose an agent incident by replaying recorded traces and fix it with idempotent tools, durable state or a budget.
- Measure cost per successful outcome and resource use for each system and set budget alerts.
