# AE-306 · Modern Data Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/practice.html

## Description

Participants build one batch pipeline end to end for Qafila, the fictional trading company of the Academy's data engineering course, whose margin report nobody trusts. They query raw extracts with analytical SQL, ingest an API and a database change feed incrementally, clean with dataframes, model a star schema with a slowly changing supplier dimension, write tested transformations and a data contract, orchestrate them, and land the result in an open table format that a second engine reads. Day four adds distributed processing, streaming and governance.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse raw transactional extracts with analytical SQL, including window functions and incremental predicates.
- Implement incremental ingestion from an API and a change feed, keeping supplier history as a slowly changing dimension.
- Design a dimensional model at a stated grain and build it as tested, version-controlled transformations.
- Build an orchestrated pipeline with a data contract, quality gates, retries and backfills that fails safely when an upstream feed breaks.
- Configure an open table format with partitioning, schema evolution and time travel, and read it from a second engine.
- Classify every field under the national classification levels and apply minimisation, masking and access rules.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- Writes SQL joins, grouping and simple window functions
- Filters and joins tables with a Python dataframe library
- Commits with Git from a shell

## Format and days

### Day 1: Store and query

- Platform shapes
- Analytical SQL on a single node
- Window functions
- Columnar files and partitioning

### Day 2: Ingest and clean

- Ingesting from APIs
- Declarative ingestion pipelines
- Change data capture, merge and history
- Cleaning with dataframes

### Day 3: Model and test

- Dimensional modelling
- Transformations as code
- Data quality tests and contracts
- Orchestration

### Day 4: Scale and production

- Open table formats
- Distributed processing when measured
- Streaming fundamentals
- Governance with PDPL and NDMO

### Day 5: Capstone: the margin mart and its defence


## Topics

### Platform shapes and analytical SQL

- Transactional and analytical systems; extract, load, transform (ELT)
- Lakehouse, layered refinement and columnar files

### Ingestion and change

- Schema drift and idempotent loads
- Change data capture (CDC), merge and slowly changing dimensions
- Single node first, distributed when measured

### Modelling, transformation and contracts

- Grain, facts and dimensions
- Tests, environments and state-aware builds
- Data contracts in an open standard
- Verifying agent-written transformations

### Orchestration, scale and streaming

- Assets, retries and backfills
- Lineage as events
- Open table formats: snapshots, schema evolution, deletion vectors, compaction
- Logs and queues, delivery guarantees, watermarks

### Governance in the pipeline

- Classification levels; Restricted, which older texts call Confidential
- Minimisation and masking under the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)
- Erasure requests against history tables and snapshots
- National Data Management Office (NDMO) quality and architecture controls

# AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/practice.html

## Description

Participants run the shared AI platform of a fictional regional health authority, where a training team, a bilingual patient-letter assistant and a nightly embedding job compete for scarce accelerators. On single-node clusters with simulated accelerators, small open-weight models and recorded traffic, they allocate and share devices, admit jobs fairly under quotas, place distributed jobs all at once, autoscale inference on the signals users feel, route requests through an inference-aware gateway, keep Restricted workloads on permitted nodes, and size capacity and cost for three hosting options. The requirements of the public Kubernetes AI conformance checklist that a simulated cluster can demonstrate serve as the acceptance rubric. Token-level cost and model routing are AE-312.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure accelerator allocation, sharing and health tainting for two tenants on a container cluster.
- Configure queues, quotas, borrowing and all-or-nothing admission for three teams.
- Optimise autoscaling of an inference service on a queue or service-objective metric, including scale to zero and cold start.
- Evaluate an inference-aware gateway against round-robin routing for goodput, latency and fairness between tenants.
- Compute memory, concurrency, replica count, power and monthly cost for a serving workload under cloud, on-premises and sovereign-provider options.
- Design a placement policy driven by data classification and audit the cluster against the conformance checklist.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- [AE-206 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-206.md)
- Deploys a containerised service to a local cluster with health probes and resource limits
- Estimates model memory from parameter count and numeric precision

## Next courses

- [AE-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-401.md)
- [AE-403 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-403.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Accelerators on a shared cluster

- Why AI workloads strain a cluster
- Requesting devices through resource claims
- Sharing and isolating devices
- Accelerator metrics

### Day 2: Queues, quotas and placement

- Admission before scheduling
- Borrowing and preemption
- Gang and topology-aware placement
- Placement under data rules

### Day 3: Serve and scale on the right signal

- Serving operators and weights as artefacts
- Why processor load is the wrong signal
- Scale to zero and cold start
- Node scaling by accelerator type

### Day 4: Route, size and cost

- Inference-aware gateways
- Priority and load shedding
- Capacity from first principles
- Cloud, on-premises or sovereign

### Day 5: Capstone: a hardened cluster and its design review


## Topics

### Accelerators as cluster resources

- Device plugins versus dynamic resource allocation
- Time-slicing, partitioning and virtualised devices
- Device health, taints and per-accelerator metrics

### Admission and scheduling

- Queues, quotas, cohorts and borrowing
- Preemption and fairness between teams
- Gang and topology-aware placement

### Serving and autoscaling

- Serving operators and model weights as registry artefacts
- Scaling pods on queue and service-objective metrics
- Scale to zero and cold start
- Node scaling by accelerator type

### Inference-aware traffic

- Endpoint picking on queue and prefix-cache state
- Priority, fairness and load shedding
- Goodput against a service objective

### Capacity, cost and placement

- Weights and key-value cache arithmetic
- Power, cooling and tokens per watt
- Rented, owned and sovereign capacity
- Classification before placement

# AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/practice.html

## Description

Participants attack and then defend a working agent: a synthetic clearance assistant for a fictional port authority that reads importers' emails and invoices, searches a tariff knowledge base, remembers each importer, runs code to compute duties and acts through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. They threat-model it, run injection, exfiltration and poisoning attacks over repeated trials, then contain it with a sandbox and egress rules, scoped short-lived delegated tokens, separated privileged and quarantined model calls, measured guardrails and approvals placed where a person adds safety. Red-team programmes are AE-407.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a threat model with data flows, trust boundaries and threats mapped to recognised risk lists and adversary-technique catalogues.
- Test the application with direct, indirect, memory and tool-poisoning attacks in Arabic and English over repeated trials.
- Design containment for generated code and outbound actions with a sandbox, an egress allowlist and recipient rules.
- Build delegated authorisation in which each tool call carries an exchanged token with one audience, a narrow scope and a short lifetime.
- Configure input guardrails and output validation and measure their false-positive and false-negative rates.
- Defend a residual-risk statement after another team attacks the hardened agent, with each confirmed finding turned into a regression test.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-207 · Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-207.md)
- [AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-302.md)
- Has built a tool-calling agent and read its traces
- Runs containers locally and changes their network settings

## Next courses

- [AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-402.md)
- [AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-407.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Model the threats

- A fooled model must break nothing important
- Data flows and trust boundaries
- Risk lists and technique catalogues
- Scoring and choosing what to test

### Day 2: Attack

- Direct and indirect injection
- Exfiltration paths
- Memory and retrieval poisoning
- Hostile tools

### Day 3: Contain

- Sandboxes for generated code
- Egress rules as capability grants
- Delegated authorisation
- Privileged and quarantined calls

### Day 4: Guard, approve and verify

- Guardrails and their error rates
- Validating outputs and tool arguments
- Approvals that people can judge
- Audit logs and regression suites

### Day 5: Capstone: red-team day and live defence


## Topics

### Threat modelling agents

- Data-flow diagrams and trust boundaries
- Private data, untrusted content and exit paths
- Model as component versus model as actor
- Risk lists, technique catalogues and scoring

### Attacks

- Direct, indirect and cross-modal injection
- Exfiltration through links, tool arguments and permitted paths
- Memory, retrieval and tool poisoning
- Success rates over repeated trials

### Containment

- Sandboxes for generated code
- An egress allowlist is a capability grant
- Read-only mounts and resolving links before path checks
- Privileged and quarantined model calls

### Identity and authorisation

- OAuth-based delegation and token exchange
- Audience, scope and lifetime
- Token passthrough and the confused deputy
- Credentials kept outside the agent's reach

### Guardrails, approvals and audit

- Classifiers and their two error rates
- Schema and policy checks on tool arguments
- Approval fatigue and where a person adds safety
- Rate limits, spend caps and a kill switch
- Action logs and security regression suites

# AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/practice.html

## Description

Participants decide when adapting a model is worth it and then do it well. For a fictional chamber of commerce whose bilingual registration requests must stay on its own servers, a prompted small open-weight model fails at field extraction and tool calls. They sort the failures, set a stronger prompted baseline, build a tuning set from traces, staff corrections and filtered teacher outputs, train low-rank adapters, distil a larger model's tool-call behaviour, evaluate against the base and a larger prompted model, and serve the result quantised with several adapters. AE-301 introduces adapters on an encoder; post-training at scale is AE-406.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse the failures of a prompted model and assign each failure class to prompting, retrieval, tuning or distillation.
- Prepare a tuning dataset from traces, corrections and teacher outputs, with template rendering, verifier filtering, deduplication, decontamination and personal-data removal.
- Configure and train low-rank adapters on a 16-bit and a 4-bit base model within the memory of one free-tier GPU.
- Evaluate the adapted model against the base and a larger prompted model with paired statistics, language slices, regression and safety checks.
- Deploy a quantised small model with several adapters and measure throughput, latency and cost per thousand requests.
- Decide whether to ship the adapted model, weighing quality, cost, licence terms and data placement.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Fine-tunes a pretrained model with a training loop or a training library
- Compares two systems on an evaluation set with a paired test

## Next courses

- [AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-406.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Decide whether to adapt

- Prompt, retrieve, tune or distil
- The baseline tuning must beat
- Licences and terms of open-weight models
- Cost and placement of the options

### Day 2: Data for tuning

- Tuning data from traces and corrections
- Teacher generation and verifier filtering
- Chat templates and tool-call formats
- Deduplication, decontamination and personal data

### Day 3: Train adapters and distil

- Low-rank adapters
- Quantised adapters and memory
- Settings that matter
- Distilling a behaviour

### Day 4: Evaluate and serve

- Paired evaluation against the base
- Regressions and safety after tuning
- One base, several adapters
- Cards and the decision memo

### Day 5: Capstone: an adapted small model and its defence


## Topics

### When to adapt

- Prompt, retrieve, tune or distil
- Tuning changes behaviour more than knowledge
- Narrow tasks small models suit and multi-step work they do not
- Licences and acceptable-use terms
- Cost and placement of each option

### Data for tuning

- Traces and staff corrections
- Teacher generation with verifier filtering
- Chat templates and tool-call formats
- Deduplication, decontamination and personal data

### Adapters and distillation

- Low-rank and quantised adapters
- Rank, learning rate and schedule
- Distilling a behaviour from a larger model

### Evaluating adapted models

- Paired comparison with the base and a larger model
- Arabic and English slices
- Forgetting and regressions
- Safety behaviour after tuning

### Serving small models

- Quantised weight formats
- Several adapters on one base model
- Throughput and cost per thousand requests

# AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise the engineer's part in deciding what to build. In a role-played engagement with a fictional regional water utility that asks for an AI assistant for leak reports, they interview call-centre and field staff about what happened last week, map the workflow and its exceptions, choose and reject use cases, write the specification as the main deliverable with acceptance criteria as evaluation cases, test the riskiest assumption with a thin prototype built with a coding agent, cost the value case, brief the utility's leadership and hand over a system the utility's own team can run.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a requested AI use case through interviews about past behaviour and a workflow map, and restate the problem where the evidence differs from the request.
- Draft a specification with users, non-goals, constraints, data classification and acceptance criteria written as evaluation cases.
- Test the riskiest assumption with a thin prototype and role-played user sessions.
- Build a value case with cost per successful task, ranges for uncertain inputs and a break-even point, and decide whether to proceed.
- Deliver a recommendation and a hand-over package to non-technical leadership and the receiving team.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-204.md)
- Has built and demonstrated a working language model application
- Writes a short technical document for a non-technical reader

## Next courses

- [AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-402.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Discover

- The engineer's job before code
- Interviews about past behaviour
- Workflows and their exceptions
- Choosing the problem

### Day 2: Specify and test

- Specification as the deliverable
- Acceptance criteria as evaluation cases
- Data, permissions and classification
- Prototype the riskiest assumption

### Day 3: Decide, communicate and hand over

- Minimum viable decisions
- The value case
- Talking to leaders
- Hand-over

### Day 4: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Discovery

- Interviews about past behaviour
- Workflows and their exceptions
- Choosing and rejecting use cases

### Specification as the deliverable

- Problem, users and non-goals
- Acceptance criteria as evaluation cases
- Data, permissions and classification

### Minimum viable decisions

- Riskiest assumption first
- Reversible and irreversible choices
- Decision records

### Value and communication

- Cost per successful task and break-even
- Ranges instead of point estimates
- Updates for leaders
- Saying what the system cannot do

### Hand-over

- Runbooks and evaluation sets
- Ownership and exit criteria
- Training the receiving team

# AE-312 · AI Cost Engineering and Model Routing

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/practice.html

## Description

Participants make the cost of language model applications measurable, attributable and smaller without losing quality. For a fictional telecom operator running three applications behind one gateway, a bilingual care assistant, a call-summary job and a billing-dispute agent, they work from a month of synthetic usage traces: they model cost per request and session, attribute spend to teams, set budgets, evaluate model tiers and reasoning settings on their own tasks, route with fallbacks, measure prefix and semantic caches, compare hosted and self-hosted serving and report cost per successful outcome. Cluster capacity planning is AE-307; engine-level optimisation is AE-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute cost per request and per session from prompt, output and cached tokens, retries, agent steps and accelerator-hours.
- Configure attribution, budgets and limits per team, application and environment on a model gateway.
- Evaluate model tiers, reasoning settings and a routing policy on the operator's own tasks, choosing by cost per successful outcome at a fixed quality floor.
- Measure how prefix and semantic caching change cost, latency and answer correctness, including isolation between customers.
- Decide between hosted APIs and a self-hosted open-weight model with a break-even analysis that includes utilisation and data-placement rules.
- Deliver a cost review with three measured savings options to engineering and finance stakeholders.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- Groups and joins usage logs with SQL or dataframes
- Has run an evaluation set against a language model application

## Format and days

### Day 1: Where the money goes

- The token cost model
- Agents, retries and long contexts
- Attribution and showback
- Budgets and limits

### Day 2: Route and cache

- Own tasks, several settings
- Routing and cascades
- Prompt layout for prefix caching
- Semantic caches and their risks

### Day 3: Host or buy, and report

- Self-hosting economics
- Batch versus interactive
- Cost per successful outcome
- The cost review

### Day 4: Capstone: the cost review, defended


## Topics

### The cost model

- Prefill, decode and cached tokens
- Retries, agent steps and context growth
- Accelerator-hours and utilisation

### Attribution and budgets

- Keys and tags per team and application
- Showback before chargeback
- No settled allocation method for multi-agent work

### Model choice and routing

- Own-task evaluation at several settings
- Cascades, tiers and fallbacks
- Cache cost of switching models

### Caching

- Prompt layout for prefix reuse
- Response and semantic caches
- Staleness and isolation between customers

### Hosting and reporting

- Self-hosting break-even
- Batch versus interactive tiers
- Cost per successful outcome
- Energy beside money

# AE-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/practice.html

## Description

Participants take the bilingual visitor assistant of a fictional national events authority, too slow at evening peaks and too costly, and make it meet its service objective at the lowest cost they can defend. They build a first-principles cost model, measure goodput curves on replayed traffic, diagnose seeded bottlenecks, then apply batching, caching, quantisation, speculative decoding, distillation, routing, disaggregated serving and autoscaling, re-running an Arabic and English task evaluation after every change.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute prefill cost, decode cost and key-value cache memory, and predict the binding resource.
- Evaluate a serving configuration by measuring its goodput curve over concurrency against latency objectives.
- Diagnose why a deployment misses its service objective and confirm the fix.
- Optimise batching, admission, prefix caching and cache precision while holding task quality.
- Evaluate quantised, distilled and speculative-decoding variants against the base model and decide which to serve.
- Design and defend a serving topology covering disaggregation, routing, replica count and scaling policy.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)
- Has served an open-weight model behind an HTTP endpoint and load-tested it
- Computes percentiles and reads a latency histogram
- Estimates memory from parameter count and numeric precision

## Format and days

### Day 1: Model the cost first

- Prefill and decode are different problems
- Key-value cache arithmetic
- Goodput against an objective
- Curves, not single numbers

### Day 2: Scheduling and caching in the engine

- Continuous batching and admission
- Long prompts slow short ones
- Prefix caching starts with prompt layout
- Semantic caching and wrong answers

### Day 3: Cheaper tokens, same quality

- Quantising weights
- Cache precision buys concurrency
- Speculative decoding
- Distilled models and routing to them

### Day 4: Across replicas and over the day

- Disaggregated prefill and decode
- Routing across replicas
- Autoscaling and cold starts
- Cost per successful request

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### The cost model of inference

- Prefill is compute-bound, decode is memory-bound
- Key-value cache arithmetic
- Roofline and queueing reasoning

### Measuring serving performance

- Time to first token, time per output token, goodput
- Profiling where a request's time goes
- Trace replay and load patterns
- Pareto curves and benchmark validity

### Inside the engine

- Continuous batching, chunked prefill, admission control
- Paged attention, cache precision and tiering
- Prefix and semantic caching; tenant isolation

### Cheaper models at the same quality

- Quantisation formats per accelerator
- Speculative decoding and acceptance rates
- Distillation and multi-adapter serving

### Across replicas and over the day

- Disaggregated prefill and decode
- Cache-aware routing
- Autoscaling, cold starts and scale to zero
- Cost per successful request and energy per token

# AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise the architect's loop on AI systems and apply it to the shared platform many teams build on. For a fictional ministry of municipal services with nine product teams and data at three classification levels, they turn requirements into measurable scenarios, draw views as code, cost three options including a non-generative one, keep a decision log, design a model catalogue, gateway, tenancy model, golden paths and showback, enforce a reference design with fitness checks, and review a peer's architecture. Serving optimisation and reliability engineering are left to AE-401 and AE-403.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare quality-attribute scenarios with measurable targets for answer quality, latency, cost, privacy and human oversight.
- Design an end-to-end architecture with context, container and data-flow views and a per-request latency and cost budget.
- Evaluate at least three solution options, including a non-generative baseline, and record the resulting decisions.
- Design a shared AI platform covering model admission, gateway, tenancy, golden paths and cost attribution.
- Design a reference architecture with fitness functions that check conformance automatically.
- Review a peer's architecture with a structured trade-off method and decide on a requested deviation.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-311.md)

# AE-403 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/practice.html

## Description

Participants set and defend reliability standards for AI services that other teams build. For a fictional postal and parcels operator running a bilingual tracking assistant on a self-hosted open-weight model with retrieval, they write service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, set admission limits with headroom from measured goodput, design and chaos-test degradation paths, lead incident drills and blameless reviews, release through canaries with automated rollback, and admit models only after verifying signatures and bills of materials.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, with error budgets and a release policy.
- Decide an admission limit and shedding priorities that keep headroom for the busiest hour.
- Design degradation for overload and dependency failure using load shedding, a smaller fallback model and a cached-answer mode.
- Lead an incident drill from detection to recovery and write a blameless review.
- Build a release gate that verifies model signatures, a bill of materials and licences before deployment.
- Review another team's AI service for production readiness and set launch conditions.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)
- Has written alerting rules on service metrics
- Runs containers on a single-node cluster
- Has released a service through a canary or blue-green rollout
- Reads a goodput-versus-concurrency curve (the measurement method is taught in AE-401)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Objectives that match what users need

- AI services fail differently
- Indicators for latency and quality
- Objectives and error budgets
- Objectives for multi-step tasks

### Day 2: Capacity and failure

- Capacity with headroom
- Admission control and shedding
- Degraded modes
- Chaos experiments

### Day 3: Incidents and safe releases

- Finding silent regressions
- Running an incident
- Canary and rollback
- Learning from incidents

### Day 4: Integrity and readiness

- The model supply chain
- Signing and verification
- Bills of materials and admission
- Production readiness reviews

### Day 5: Readiness review defences


## Topics

### Objectives for AI services

- Time to first token, time per output token, availability
- Answer quality from sampled online grading
- Error budgets and release policy
- Objectives for multi-step tasks

### Capacity under load

- Queueing and tail latency
- Headroom for the busiest hour
- Admission control and load shedding

### Designing for failure

- Provider, retrieval and tool failures
- Fallback models and degraded modes
- Retry storms and chaos experiments

### Incidents and releases

- Burn-rate alerts on latency and quality
- Incident roles and decision logs
- Canary releases with automated rollback
- Reviews turned into regression tests

### Integrity and readiness

- Signing a manifest of hashed model files
- Machine learning bills of materials and licences
- Admission policy at deployment
- Readiness reviews and launch conditions

# AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/practice.html

## Description

Participants design how an organisation decides that an AI system is good enough to release, and how it keeps knowing afterwards. For the fictional Wadi Noor Utilities (a bilingual customer assistant, a complaint-triage classifier, a meter-anomaly model and an internal coding agent) they tier systems by risk, report results with clustered, paired and grader-corrected uncertainty, audit a public benchmark before it informs a model choice, write and back-test release criteria, turn incidents into regression cases and brief a mock board. All logs, traces and incidents are synthetic. Single-system gates are AE-303; service objectives are AE-403.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute clustered, paired and grader-corrected intervals for evaluation results and the number of items needed to detect a stated effect.
- Design a risk-tiered evaluation programme that states the evidence each tier needs before and after release.
- Audit a public benchmark for construct validity, label errors, contamination signals and sensitivity to harness and token budget.
- Specify blocking and advisory release criteria with non-inferiority margins and back-test them against history.
- Design post-release monitoring that grades sampled production traffic and turns incidents into regression cases.
- Defend a release recommendation with its uncertainty, residual risk and cost before a decision board.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- Computes a bootstrap interval and a paired difference in Python
- Has maintained an evaluation suite or release gate for a deployed system

## Format and days

### Day 1: Evaluation as a system

- An inventory comes before a suite
- Tiering by impact, autonomy and reach
- The evidence each tier needs
- A shared harness and dataset registry

### Day 2: Statistics of evaluations

- Items are a sample
- Repeated trials
- Paired comparisons and power
- Graders are instruments

### Day 3: Benchmarks and release criteria

- Auditing a public benchmark
- Harness and budget effects
- Writing release criteria
- Back-testing criteria

### Day 4: After release and to the board

- Change classes and exceptions
- Monitoring that feeds the suite
- Scorecards with uncertainty
- Briefing a release board

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Evaluation as an organisational system

- Inventory of systems and owners
- Tiering by impact, autonomy and reach
- Evidence per tier: capability, regression, adversarial, subgroup, human review
- Shared harness, dataset registry and grader records

### Statistics of evaluations

- Items as a sample and clustered standard errors
- Repeated trials and consistency
- Paired comparisons, power and minimum effect
- Correcting pass rates for grader error

### Auditing benchmarks and claims

- Construct validity and task ambiguity
- Contamination and models that recognise a test
- Harness, token budget and infrastructure effects on rankings

### Release criteria

- Blocking and advisory checks
- Non-inferiority margins and noise floors
- Change classes: prompt, model, retrieval, tool, provider
- Sign-off, exceptions and their expiry

### After release and reporting

- Sampled grading of production traffic
- Incidents turned into regression cases
- Scorecards with uncertainty, residual risk and cost
- Linking gates to the national risk framework

# AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/practice.html

## Description

Participants post-train open-weight models on domain data and prove the result is worth serving. For the fictional Eastern Coast Permits Authority they turn synthetic bilingual permit records, officer edits and agent traces into tuning mixtures, then run full and sharded supervised tuning, preference optimisation, a short reinforcement learning loop with verifiable rewards, distillation from a larger teacher and tuning on filtered agent traces. Each model is compared with its base and a prompting and retrieval baseline, for task gains and for regressions in general ability, safety and Arabic quality. AE-310 covers single-GPU adapters and serving; this course goes beyond them.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Decide whether post-training is justified over prompting and retrieval for a task, and which method fits it.
- Build a validated tuning mixture of domain records, teacher-generated examples and general data with licence, deduplication and leakage checks.
- Configure supervised tuning at scale, choosing full-parameter or adapter tuning and a sharding strategy that fit a stated accelerator memory budget.
- Train with preference data or verifiable rewards and diagnose reward hacking in the result.
- Produce a small model by distillation and by tuning on outcome-filtered agent traces that meets a latency and cost target.
- Evaluate an adapted model against its base for task improvement and for regressions in general ability, safety and Arabic dialect quality.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Writes and debugs a training loop in a deep-learning framework
- Has tuned a model with adapters and evaluated it against its base

## Format and days

### Day 1: Data decides the result

- When post-training beats prompting and retrieval
- Data mixtures against forgetting
- Synthetic data and its validation
- Memory and compute accounting

### Day 2: Supervised tuning

- Full tuning against adapters
- Hyperparameters that matter
- Forgetting and regressions
- Scaling out

### Day 3: Preferences and rewards

- Preference data from expert edits
- Direct preference optimisation
- Verifiable rewards
- Reward hacking

### Day 4: Distillation, traces and the decision

- Distilling a teacher
- Training on agent traces
- Merging task adapters
- Evaluating the adapted model

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Deciding to post-train

- Prompting, retrieval and tuning as alternatives
- Cost of training against cost of serving
- Open-weight licences and acceptable-use terms

### Data for post-training

- Curation, deduplication and mixing against forgetting
- Synthetic data from teachers and its validation
- Leakage against evaluation sets

### Supervised tuning at scale

- Full tuning, adapters and quantised adapters
- Memory accounting for weights, gradients and optimiser state
- Sharded multi-GPU training
- Forgetting and safety regressions

### Preferences and rewards

- Preference pairs and annotator agreement
- Direct preference optimisation and its variants
- Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
- Reward hacking

### Distillation, traces and merging

- Distillation from a teacher
- Rejection sampling of agent traces
- Merging methods and interference between tasks

### Evaluating adapted models

- Task, general, safety and Arabic dialect slices
- Paired comparison with the base
- Model cards for adapted models

# AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/practice.html

## Description

Participants lead the assurance of AI systems that act on an organisation's data. For the fictional Northern Region Benefits Agency (a bilingual benefits assistant and a case-worker agent that reads case files and drafts letters) they plan and run a red-team exercise in Arabic and English, manually and with automated probes, assess the risks with the National AI Risk Management Framework, review the security architecture for agent identity, least privilege, isolation and egress, and assemble an assurance case that ends in a residual-risk briefing. Targets run in a sandbox on synthetic case data. Hardening a single application is AE-308.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Plan a red-team exercise with objectives tied to harms, scope, rules of engagement and stop conditions.
- Conduct manual and automated adversarial testing in Arabic and English and quantify attack success over repeated trials.
- Assess the risks of an agent with the national framework, from context to treatment and residual sign-off.
- Review a security architecture for agent identity, delegated authority, least privilege, isolation and egress control.
- Build an assurance case that links each claim to evidence and maps the evidence to a control framework.
- Present residual risk and a recommendation with conditions to an accountable executive.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Has written a threat model for a system they built
- Reads a risk register and a likelihood and impact matrix

## Format and days

### Day 1: Plan the exercise

- Assurance is an argument with evidence
- Scoping from the threat model
- Objectives, scope and rules of engagement
- Choosing techniques from catalogues

### Day 2: Run the red team

- Manual probing in two languages
- Indirect injection and goal hijack
- Automated campaigns over repeated trials
- Findings people can act on

### Day 3: Assess the risk

- The national framework as method
- Scoring and calibration
- Treatment and residual risk
- Supplier and model-change risk

### Day 4: Review and assemble the evidence

- Security architecture review
- Identity and delegated authority
- Assurance evidence packs
- Briefing the accountable executive

### Day 5: Capstone: an assurance pack and its defence


## Topics

### Assurance as argument

- Claims, arguments and evidence
- Independence of testers and reviewers
- Evidence that defeats a claim

### Red-team practice

- Objectives, rules of engagement and stop conditions
- Technique catalogues: OWASP lists and MITRE ATLAS
- Arabic, dialect and transliteration attacks
- Automated probing and success over trials
- Findings turned into regression tests

### Risk assessment with the national framework

- Context and scope
- The seven risk categories
- Likelihood and impact scoring and calibration
- Treatment and residual sign-off
- Supplier and model-change risk

### Security architecture review

- Agent identity and delegated authority
- Least privilege derived from data classification
- Isolation tiers and egress control
- Action-level monitoring and kill switches

### Evidence and reporting

- Crosswalks to ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and the CSA AI Controls Matrix
- Assurance cases and gap lists
- Briefing accountable executives

# AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- On the learning path: [AI Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and evaluate applications that see, listen and speak, with Arabic as the main case. For the fictional Heritage Trails Authority they extract grounded fields from visitor and ranger photos with vision-language models, benchmark open-weight speech recognisers on dialects and code-switched speech, test synthesised read-back, and assemble a bilingual voice booking line with turn-taking, interruption and tool calls within a latency budget. They test it with simulated callers and choose between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on measured quality, latency and cost. Photos are public-domain or synthetic; calls use synthetic voices and public speech corpora.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement image applications with vision-language models that return validated structured fields grounded in the image.
- Evaluate speech recognisers on Arabic dialects and code-switched speech with explicit normalisation rules.
- Build a bilingual voice agent that handles turn-taking, interruption and confirmed tool calls within a latency budget.
- Diagnose failure modes specific to image and audio inputs, including invented objects, text produced on silence and instructions hidden in images.
- Design a multimodal test set and an end-to-end evaluation with simulated callers.
- Decide between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on quality, latency and cost per call.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-301 · Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-301.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Has built a language model application with structured outputs and tool calls
- Computes precision, recall and an error rate with an interval

## Format and days

### Day 1: Seeing

- How a vision-language model sees
- Structured extraction from photos
- Grounding answers in pixels
- Arabic text and hidden instructions

### Day 2: Listening

- From waveform to text
- Normalisation decides the error rate
- Dialects and code-switching
- Streaming and silence

### Day 3: Speaking

- Synthesis and read-back
- Cascaded versus speech-to-speech
- Turn-taking and interruption
- Tool calls during speech

### Day 4: Evaluating and choosing

- Multimodal test sets
- Simulated callers
- Choosing by quality, latency and cost
- Voice, faces and consent

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Vision-language models in applications

- Visual tokens, resolution and cost
- Structured extraction from photos
- Grounding with boxes and points
- Frames from video
- Instructions hidden in images

### Speech recognition

- Recogniser families and multilingual encoders
- Arabic normalisation of diacritics, letter variants and numerals
- Dialects, code-switching and telephone audio
- Streaming, voice activity detection, diarisation and text on silence

### Synthesis and voice agents

- Read-back of names, numbers and dates
- Cascaded, speech-to-speech and full-duplex designs
- End-of-turn detection and interruption
- Latency budgets and tool calls during speech

### Evaluation

- Multimodal test sets
- Error rates with intervals by slice
- Simulated callers
- Cost per call

### Responsible voice and image handling

- Voice and faces as personal data
- Consent, retention and minimisation
- Disclosure of synthetic voices

# DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-201/practice.html

## Description

Participants learn inference by computing it. On synthetic data from a fictional water utility whose true population is known, they draw repeated samples, build bootstrap intervals, run permutation tests beside classical ones, and report effect sizes with intervals instead of bare p-values. They see how testing 30 districts at once produces false findings and correct for it, then fit and read a first linear regression.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain what a sampling distribution, a standard error, a confidence interval and a p-value describe, and identify common misreadings.
- Compute bootstrap intervals for a mean, a median and a group difference, resampling the correct unit.
- Implement a permutation test, compare it with the matching classical test and report an effect size with an interval.
- Apply family-wise and false discovery rate corrections to many tests and measure the false findings without them.
- Analyse a linear regression of water consumption on household size and temperature, with slope intervals and residual checks.
- Deliver an inference brief that answers a manager's question with an estimate, an interval, a test, an effect size and stated limits.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- Filters and groups a table with a dataframe library
- Computes a mean, a standard deviation and a simple probability

## Next courses

- [DS-203 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-203.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)
- [DS-205 · Designing and Reading Experiments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-205.md)
- [DS-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-301.md)
- [DS-302 · Online Experiments and A/B Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-302.md)
- [DS-304 · Forecasting and Time Series](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-304.md)
- [DS-308 · Data Storytelling and Decision Briefings](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-308.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Variation

- A sample is one draw of many
- Standard error by simulation and by formula
- Skew, outliers and the median
- Describing a sample honestly

### Day 2: Intervals

- The bootstrap idea
- Coverage is a testable claim
- Resample the right unit
- Intervals for differences and ratios

### Day 3: Tests

- A test is a shuffling rule
- p-values and their misreadings
- Effect size and practical significance
- Thirty districts, many false alarms

### Day 4: Regression and reporting

- Least squares as a summary
- Slopes with intervals
- Residuals and confounding
- Writing an inference brief

### Day 5: Capstone: the inference brief and its defence


## Topics

### Variation and estimation

- Population, sample, parameter and statistic
- Sampling distributions and standard error
- Skew, outliers and the median

### Bootstrap intervals

- Resampling the right unit
- Percentile intervals and coverage
- When the bootstrap fails

### Testing

- The null hypothesis as a shuffling rule
- Classical tests as approximations
- What a p-value is and is not
- Effect size, Type I and Type II errors

### Many comparisons

- Forking paths
- Family-wise error and false discovery rate
- Analysis plans written before the data

### A first regression

- Least squares and slope intervals
- Residual checks
- Confounding and a second variable

---

# DS-202 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-202/practice.html

## Description

Participants assemble an analysis dataset for a fictional food bank network from four sources: registrations with personal data, branch logs, a donations API and open population data. They record provenance, join with key and cardinality checks, clean Arabic and English text, dates and units, write validation rules that rerun on every build, and measure how missing data and measurement error move a headline estimate. Personal data are minimised and pseudonymised, and the dataset rebuilds from raw sources with one command.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe missing-data mechanisms and kinds of measurement error and the bias each can introduce.
- Prepare a provenance record per source covering origin, owner, coverage, sharing basis, refresh date and limits.
- Implement joins with key checks, cardinality tests and reconciliation counts so that no row is silently lost or duplicated.
- Configure validation rules for types, ranges, uniqueness, completeness and cross-field consistency that run on every rebuild.
- Analyse how complete-case analysis, imputation and a sensitivity range change a headline estimate.
- Build a rebuildable analysis dataset from raw sources with personal data minimised and pseudonymised.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- Writes SQL joins and group-by queries without assistance

## Next courses

- [DS-306 · Text and Unstructured Data for Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-306.md)
- [DS-311 · Data Quality, Labelling and Pipelines for Analysis](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-311.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Find and document the sources

- Start from the question, not the files
- Files, APIs and databases
- Provenance and sharing basis
- Coverage and sampling frames

### Day 2: Join and clean

- Encodings and Arabic text
- Keys and cardinality
- Matching without a clean key
- Types, units and dates

### Day 3: Missing data and measurement

- Why data go missing
- Imputation and its cost
- Sensitivity ranges
- Measurement error and proxies

### Day 4: Validate and protect

- Quality dimensions as rules
- Cross-field and cross-source checks
- Minimise and pseudonymise

# DS-203 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-203/practice.html

## Description

Participants answer a fictional regional tourism board's questions by exploring its data, starting every analysis from written questions. They profile tables, examine distributions, relationships and change over time, build charts with a grammar of graphics and scales that do not mislead, and test by resampling whether a pattern could be chance. They repair misleading charts and write findings that state what is and is not shown, in a notebook that reruns from raw data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analysis and explain why a pattern found by exploring needs a fresh test.
- Prepare an analysis plan listing questions, units of observation, variables and the comparison that answers each.
- Analyse distributions, relationships and change over time with summaries and charts suited to each variable type.
- Use a grammar of graphics to map variables to position, colour and facets with honest scales, baselines and labels.
- Test whether an apparent difference or correlation could arise by chance, using permutation or bootstrap resampling.
- Deliver a reproducible exploratory report that states findings, uncertainty, open questions and limits for a non-specialist reader.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- Makes a basic chart in any plotting library

## Next courses

- [DS-307 · Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-307.md)
- [DS-308 · Data Storytelling and Decision Briefings](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-308.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Questions and first looks

- Write the questions first
- Profiling a table
- Distributions
- Summaries that fit the shape

### Day 2: Relationships and time

- Two variables at once
- Counts, rates and denominators
- Change over time
- When the total reverses

### Day 3: Building honest charts

- Marks, encodings and scales
- Small multiples
- Charts that mislead
- Colour, labels and Arabic text

### Day 4: Check and report

- Could it be chance
- Showing uncertainty
- The traps of exploring
- A report that reruns

### Day 5: Capstone: the exploratory report and its defence


## Topics

### Questions before charts

- Analysis plans and units of observation
- Exploratory versus confirmatory work
- Profiling a new table

### Distributions and relationships

- Histograms, density and box plots
- Scatter plots and overplotting
- Rates and denominators
- Change over time and seasonality

### Grammar of graphics

- Marks, encodings and scales
- Small multiples
- Colour-blind-safe palettes
- Arabic and bilingual labels

### Honest charts

- Baselines and axis ranges

- Showing uncertainty

# DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-204/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-204/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-204/practice.html

## Description

Participants predict which trainees of a fictional vocational training fund are likely not to complete, so that advisers can offer support early. On synthetic enrolment data with repeated trainees and cohorts, they climb a baseline ladder to tuned gradient-boosted trees, test an automated or pretrained challenger, choose validation that mirrors use, audit for leakage, set a threshold, break errors down by subgroup and write a model card. Deployment is left to AE-205 and AE-305.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify the leakage type and the fitting validation scheme in short tabular modelling cases.
- Apply a baseline ladder from a constant predictor to tuned gradient-boosted trees, logging every run.
- Implement validation that matches the data structure and measure how far a random split overstates performance.
- Test an automated or pretrained challenger against the tuned model under identical folds and time budget.
- Analyse calibration, the decision threshold and held-out errors by subgroup, with intervals that reflect slice size.
- Build a validated tabular model from framing to model card and defend its validation scheme and limits.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)

- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- Joins and groups tables with a dataframe library
- Explains overfitting and the purpose of a held-out set

## Next courses

- [DS-305 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-305.md)

- [DS-309 · Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-309.md)
- [DS-310 · Problem Framing and Analytical Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-310.md)

- A prediction serves a decision
- The baseline ladder
- Linear models first
- Features from history

- Gradient-boosted trees
- Tuning under a budget
- Automated and pretrained challengers

# DS-205 · Designing and Reading Experiments

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-205/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-205/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-205/practice.html

## Description

Participants design randomised experiments for a fictional municipal permits office and read the results without fooling themselves. They turn a decision question into a pre-registration with a hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, a stop rule and a unit of randomisation, compute sample size by formula and by simulation, analyse a synthetic experiment log, check that randomisation worked, and measure how peeking, many metrics and a mismatched unit inflate false wins. Variance reduction and sequential tests are left to DS-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish a randomised experiment, a quasi-experiment and an observational comparison, and explain the causal claim each supports.
- Draft a pre-registration stating the decision, hypothesis, unit of randomisation, primary and guardrail metrics, stop rule and analysis plan.
- Compute the sample size and run time needed to detect a minimum effect of interest and check it by simulation.
- Analyse a completed two-arm experiment with a difference in proportions, a confidence interval and a sample ratio mismatch test.
- Measure by simulation the false-positive rate caused by peeking, many metrics and analysis at the wrong unit.
- Review a reported experiment and decide whether it supports the decision it claims to support.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- Computes a proportion, a difference in means and a confidence interval
- Writes a simulation loop in Python or R

## Next courses

- [DS-302 · Online Experiments and A/B Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-302.md)
- [DS-303 · Causal Inference from Observational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-303.md)
- [DS-310 · Problem Framing and Analytical Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-310.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Design

- Which claims need an experiment
- Decision, hypothesis and metrics
- Choosing the unit of randomisation
- Pre-registration

### Day 2: Size and run

- Power and the minimum effect
- Power by simulation
- Cluster randomisation
- Run time and seasonality

### Day 3: Read the result

- Did randomisation work
- Estimate, interval and effect
- False wins by simulation
- Reviewing a reported result

### Day 4: Capstone: the design and analysis pack and its defence


## Topics

### From decision to design

- Decision, hypothesis and estimand
- Primary, secondary and guardrail metrics
- Pre-registration and stop rules

### Randomisation

- Simple, stratified and cluster assignment
- Balance and sample ratio checks
- Interference between units

### Sample size and power

- Minimum effect of interest
- Formula and simulation
- Run time and weekly cycles

### Reading a result

- Differences, intervals and effect sizes
- Practical against statistical significance
- Subgroups read with care

### Common traps

- Peeking
- Many metrics
- Wrong unit of analysis
- Novelty effects and attrition

# DS-206 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-206/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-206/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-206/practice.html

## Description

Participants analyse data with a coding assistant or agent in a notebook and stay accountable for every number. For a fictional courier company they decide which steps to delegate, brief the assistant with acceptance checks, prove results by recomputing key numbers another way, measure how answers vary between runs, decide which data may go to which assistant, and package an analysis that a peer reruns from logged prompts, code and data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify which analysis steps suit delegation and which need the analyst's own judgement, with a reason for each.
- Prepare a delegation brief stating question, data, definitions, constraints and acceptance checks before the assistant runs.
- Test assisted analyses by recomputing headline numbers another way and checking joins, filters, denominators and chart encodings.
- Measure run-to-run variability by repeating one request five times and comparing code, numbers and conclusions.
- Classify analysis data by sensitivity and assign each table to a local assistant, a hosted assistant or neither.
- Deliver an assisted analysis package that another analyst can rerun and audit from logged prompts, code, data and verification notes.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- Writes SQL joins and dataframe group-bys without assistance
- Has completed one analysis end to end, from raw table to chart

## Format and days

### Day 1: Delegate with intent

- What assistants get wrong in analysis
- Delegate, assist or keep
- The delegation brief
- Context files for a project

### Day 2: Verify

- Recompute it another way
- Joins, filters and denominators
- Charts and words
- Ask it twice

### Day 3: Reproduce and disclose

- Which data may go where
- Logging assisted work
- The peer rerun
- Disclosing assistance

### Day 4: Capstone: the assisted analysis package and its defence


## Topics

### What to delegate

- Where assistants and agents fail in data work
- Evidence that unchecked delegation erodes skill
- Delegate, assist or keep

### Briefing an assistant

- Acceptance checks
- Project context files
- Small steps with checkpoints

### Verification

- Recomputing another way
- Join, filter and denominator checks
- Charts and summaries against the data

### Variability and reproducibility

- Asking twice
- Logging models, settings and prompts

### Data handling and disclosure

- What may go to which assistant
- Disclosing assistance in a report

# DS-207 · Responsible Data Practice and Conduct in Analytical Work

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-200.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-207/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-207/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-207/practice.html

## Description

Participants handle an analytical engagement for a fictional university's student-success unit. They test requests against the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), classify the data and decide what may be shared with a government partner, suppress small cells in aggregate outputs, compare outcome and error rates across student groups, keep an analysis log and a datasheet, and handle three stakeholder conversations: scoping, pushing back on an unsafe request and explaining limits. Deeper de-identification and fairness audits are in DS-309.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the PDPL principles and the classification and sharing rules an analysis engages, from lawful basis to data subjects' rights and transfer.
- Classify the datasets and outputs of an analysis and decide what may be shared, with whom and in what form.
- Apply aggregation and small-cell suppression to results tables and check that no student can be singled out.
- Analyse referral and error rates across student groups and report differences with their uncertainty and possible causes.
- Prepare a datasheet and an analysis log that let a reviewer trace each result to its data, decisions and approvals.
- Lead a stakeholder conversation that rescopes an unsafe or unclear request into a lawful, answerable question, and record the agreement.

## Prerequisites

- Computes rates and a confidence interval for a proportion by group in SQL or a dataframe

# DS-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-301/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-301/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-301/practice.html

## Description

Participants build regression models that answer a stated question and defend what each term means. On synthetic data from Sahil Water, a fictional utility with 30 districts, they fit linear models with splines and interactions, logistic models for late payment and count models for leak reports, diagnose misfit by simulating from the fit, handle grouped data with clustered errors and random intercepts, and penalise many predictors. Results are reported as marginal effects with intervals.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement linear models with interactions and splines and report average marginal effects with intervals.
- Apply logistic and count models, choosing between Poisson and negative binomial from a dispersion check.
- Diagnose misfit with residuals, influence measures and simulation from the fitted model, then correct the model.
- Analyse grouped data with clustered standard errors and a random-intercept model and explain how the intervals change.
- Apply ridge and lasso with cross-validated tuning and measure the stability of the selected predictors.
- Build and defend a regression model for a planner's question, justifying terms, family, uncertainty and whether the use is descriptive, predictive or causal.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
