# DS-303 · Causal Inference from Observational Data

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-303/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-303/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-303/practice.html

## Description

Participants answer causal questions where no experiment was run. For the Rimal Employment Fund, a fictional agency whose wage subsidy reached regions in different years, they write each question as an estimand, draw a causal graph to decide what to adjust for, and estimate effects with matching and weighting, staggered difference-in-differences, synthetic control and regression discontinuity. The synthetic data carry known true effects, and each analysis ends with a sensitivity analysis and a plain list of assumptions.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Draft a causal graph (directed acyclic graph, DAG) and derive a valid adjustment set, naming colliders and bad controls.
- Apply propensity-score matching and inverse probability weighting with overlap and balance checks.
- Apply difference-in-differences with a leads-and-lags plot and an estimator suited to staggered adoption.
- Implement synthetic control and regression discontinuity, each with its standard diagnostic.
- Defend an identification strategy for a new causal question against at least two alternatives.
- Evaluate an estimate's sensitivity to unmeasured confounding and state how strong a confounder would need to be to overturn it.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-205 · Designing and Reading Experiments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-205.md)
- [DS-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-301.md)
- Explains why randomisation removes confounding

## Next courses

- [DS-406 · Measuring the Impact of Data and AI Programmes](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-406.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Questions, estimands and graphs

# DS-304 · Forecasting and Time Series

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-304/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-304/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-304/practice.html

## Description

Participants forecast with the discipline of a backtest. On synthetic daily electricity demand from Shams Power, a fictional distributor with 12 regions and 400 feeders, they decompose series, set a seasonal-naive benchmark floor, fit exponential smoothing and ARIMA-family models with weather and Hijri holidays, train one boosted model across many series, reconcile feeder and regional forecasts and run pretrained zero-shot forecasters as baselines. Every method is scored by rolling-origin cross-validation with point and probabilistic measures and reaches the planner as a fan chart.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply decomposition and a seasonal-naive benchmark floor scored by rolling-origin cross-validation.
- Implement exponential smoothing, ARIMA-family and dynamic regression models with temperature and moving-holiday terms.
- Measure point and quantile accuracy of a global boosted model and a pretrained zero-shot forecaster against statistical models.
- Review a forecast evaluation for leakage across time and selection on the test window, and correct it.
- Build a forecasting analysis for new series and defend method, horizon and uncertainty to a planner.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-201.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)
- Resamples and reshapes time-indexed data in a dataframe

## Next courses

- [DS-404 · Advanced Modelling for Structured Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-404.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Look, frame and set the floor

- What is forecast, and why
- Seeing structure
- Decomposition
- The benchmark floor

### Day 2: Statistical forecasters

- Exponential smoothing
- ARIMA-family models
- Weather and moving holidays
- Intervals that hold

### Day 3: Many series and pretrained models

- Many series and hierarchies
- Global boosted forecasters
- Pretrained zero-shot forecasters
- Choosing among families

### Day 4: Review and communicate

- Leakage across time
- New and short series
- Combining forecasts
- Fan charts and forecast notes

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Framing and structure

- Horizon and the decision served
- Seasonality and Hijri moving holidays
- Decomposition

### Evaluation

- Benchmark floors
- Rolling-origin cross-validation
- Scaled errors and pinball loss
- Leakage across time

### Forecasters

- Exponential smoothing and ARIMA
- Dynamic regression
- Global models across series
- Hierarchical reconciliation
- Zero-shot pretrained models and their licences

### Communicating forecasts

- Interval coverage
- Fan charts
- Notes for planners

# DS-305 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-305/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-305/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-305/practice.html

## Description

Participants produce the evidence an independent validator needs about a trained model: whether its probabilities can be trusted, how wide its errors are, what drives its predictions, where it stops working and whom it fails. For Mizan Community Lending, a fictional microfinance lender, they repair calibration, wrap models in conformal intervals and prediction sets, test coverage by subgroup and under shift, show where explanations mislead, tabulate subgroup error and write a validation report against a published checklist. Fairness mitigation and documentation are DS-309.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Measure calibration with proper scores and reliability diagrams, recalibrate, and report the effect by subgroup.
- Implement conformal intervals and prediction sets and test coverage overall, by subgroup and under simulated shift.
- Apply permutation, accumulated-local-effect and Shapley-value explanations and test their stability across refits.
- Diagnose why a model degrades on a later batch from slice metrics, coverage loss and changed explanations.
- Audit a model package for conceptual soundness, outcome performance and monitoring readiness and decide whether it is fit for use.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)
- [DS-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-301.md)
- Trains and cross-validates a gradient-boosted classifier

## Next courses

- [DS-403 · Statistical Evaluation of AI Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-403.md)
- [DS-404 · Advanced Modelling for Structured Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-404.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Can the probabilities be trusted

- What a validator needs
- Proper scores and reliability
- Recalibration
- Calibration by subgroup

### Day 2: Intervals with guarantees

- Conformal intervals
- Prediction sets
- Coverage by group
- Coverage under shift

### Day 3: What drives the predictions

- Permutation importance
- Effect plots
- Shapley values
- When explanations mislead

### Day 4: Validate and decide

- Subgroup validation
- Diagnosing degradation
- Checklists and model cards
- The fit-for-use decision

### Day 5: Capstone: an independent validation


## Topics

### What validation must show

- Conceptual soundness, outcome analysis and monitoring
- Guarantees and assumptions
- Checklists and model cards

### Calibration

- Proper scoring rules
- Reliability diagrams
- Recalibration
- Calibration by subgroup

### Conformal prediction

- Exchangeability
- Split conformal intervals
- Prediction sets
- Coverage by group and under shift

### Explanations and their limits

- Permutation importance
- Partial dependence and accumulated local effects
- Shapley values
- Correlated features

### Subgroups, shift and conditions of use

- Subgroup performance as validation evidence
- Diagnosing degradation

# DS-306 · Text and Unstructured Data for Data Science

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-306/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-306/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-306/practice.html

## Description

Participants turn text into measurements they can defend. For the Sada Citizen Voice Centre, a fictional agency receiving complaints in Arabic and English, they normalise Arabic script and dialect spellings, redact personal data, build sparse and embedding-based classifiers, classify and extract fields with a prompted open-weight language model, and treat every model-made label as a measurement: agreement with a human gold set, stability across runs and prompts, gaps between dialects and the bias it carries into estimates. Writing labelling guidelines and adjudication are in DS-311.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a bilingual corpus by normalising script, removing near-duplicates and redacting personal data.
- Implement sparse, embedding-based and prompted classifiers and score them on one held-out gold set.
- Implement schema-constrained field extraction and measure field-level precision and recall.
- Compute a district complaint rate from model labels corrected with a human-labelled sample and compare it with the uncorrected rate.
- Evaluate a language model as an annotator and decide whether its labels can feed a downstream estimate.
- Design a text-measurement pipeline for a stakeholder question and defend each measurement choice.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-202 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-202.md)
- [DS-204 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-204.md)
- Calls a web API from Python and parses JSON

## Format and days

### Day 1: Text into clean data

- Text as a data source
- Preparing Arabic text
- Near-duplicates
- Redacting personal data

### Day 2: Labels you can trust

- Gold sets and agreement
- Sparse baselines
- Embeddings as features
- Comparing classifiers fairly

### Day 3: Language models as instruments

- Prompted classification
- Ask it twice
- Dialect gaps
- Is the model a good annotator

### Day 4: From documents to tables

- Schema-constrained extraction
- Field-level validation
- Structure in text
- Errors downstream

### Day 5: Capstone: a text measurement defended live


## Topics

### Text as data

- Document sources and sampling
- Arabic normalisation and dialects
- Near-duplicates
- Redaction

### Labels as measurement

- Gold sets from a supplied codebook
- Chance-corrected agreement
- Reliability of model-made labels

### Representations and language models

- Sparse and embedding features
- Prompted classification
- Schema-constrained extraction
- Run and prompt stability

### From text to tables

- Field-level validation
- Correcting downstream estimates with a human sample
- Version records

# DS-307 · Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-307/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-307/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-307/practice.html

## Description

Participants take over performance reporting for Wadi Noor Transit, a fictional bus operator whose three reports give three different on-time figures. On a synthetic warehouse of trips, boardings and routes they write governed metric definitions, build a semantic model that defines each metric once, design a dashboard for one decision within a load-time budget, trace an anomaly to its source, and test a conversational analytics agent on certified questions with and without the semantic layer.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why reports built on one warehouse disagree on the same measure.
- Draft metric definitions stating formula, grain, filters, time logic, owner and limits.
- Implement a star-schema semantic model with a slowly changing route dimension and each metric defined once.
- Analyse a metric anomaly by drill-down and segmentation to find its source.
- Design a dashboard for a named audience and decision within a load-time budget.
- Evaluate a conversational analytics agent against governed metrics and decide which question types it may answer unreviewed.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [DS-203 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-203.md)
- Writes SQL with joins, grouping and window functions
- Has built a chart-based report for others

## Format and days

- Why three reports disagree
- Anatomy of a metric definition
- Ratios, distinct counts and time logic
- Metric trees

### Day 2: Model once

- Star schemas for analysis
- Changing dimensions and calendars
- Fan-out and join paths
- Metrics in an open specification

### Day 3: Show and investigate

- Dashboards start from a decision
- Comparisons and bilingual layout
- Load time is a design constraint
- Investigating an anomaly

### Day 4: Let an agent answer

- From question to query
- Certified questions
- With and without the semantic layer
- What the agent may answer

### Day 5: Capstone: fares and concessions


## Topics

### Metrics

- Rates, ratios, distinct counts and snapshots
- Grain, time windows, Hijri and Gregorian calendars
- Metric trees, owners and change control

### Semantic models

- Star schemas and slowly changing dimensions
- Join paths and fan-out errors
- Metrics in an open interchange specification

### Dashboard design

- Audience, decision and comparisons
- Right-to-left layouts and accessibility
- Pre-aggregation and load-time budgets

### Investigating a metric

- Drill-down and segmentation
- Mix shift and Simpson's paradox

### Conversational analytics

- Certified questions, including ones to refuse
- Wrong grain, wrong filter, invented metric

# DS-308 · Data Storytelling and Decision Briefings

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)

- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-308/practice.html

## Description

Participants turn a completed analysis into a recommendation a decision maker can act on. Analysts at Al-Nakhla Health Cluster, a fictional regional health provider, have finished a study of missed outpatient appointments and a text-reminder pilot. Participants frame the decision, build an answer-first storyline from fourteen findings of mixed value, redesign exploratory charts to explain, state uncertainty in plain Arabic and English, write a two-page decision memo and give an assessed live briefing to a panel playing the cluster's executives. Chart construction is DS-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a decision context to name the decision maker, options, criteria and the evidence that would change the choice.
- Draft an answer-first storyline that groups and orders the supporting reasons and discards weak findings.
- Prepare explanatory charts whose titles state the finding, annotated for one message in Arabic and English.
- Draft plain-language statements of uncertainty, assumptions and risks using ranges, natural frequencies and scenarios.
- Deliver a decision memo stating recommendation, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives and what to monitor.
- Defend a recommendation in a live briefing under questioning.

# DS-309 · Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-309/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-309/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-309/practice.html

## Description

Participants take the synthetic applicant data and eligibility-screening model of Yusr Housing Support Fund, a fictional public fund, through the checks a release needs: they measure re-identification risk and de-identify the table, publish differentially private counts under a budget, test a synthetic extract for leakage, audit subgroup errors against the bias types in SDAIA's AI Bias Reference Guide, and write the datasheet, model card and impact assessment a reviewer needs. Calibration and explanation are DS-305.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish pseudonymisation, de-identification, aggregation, synthetic data and differential privacy by the guarantee and cost of each.
- Measure re-identification risk from quasi-identifiers and reduce it while tracking analytic utility.
- Compute differentially private counts and means and state the accuracy cost of a privacy budget.
- Test a synthetic extract for analytic utility and membership-inference leakage.
- Audit a screening model for subgroup disparities, choose fairness criteria that fit the decision and evaluate two mitigations.
- Build the datasheet, model card and impact assessment a reviewer needs to judge and rerun a release.

- [DS-207 · Responsible Data Practice and Conduct in Analytical Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-207.md)

# DS-310 · Problem Framing and Analytical Review

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)

## Description

Participants practise the work before and after an analysis, using requests from Ghadeer Water Company, a fictional water utility. - Design an analysis plan stating data, method, threats to validity and the result that would change the decision.
- Review an analysis for errors in question fit, data handling, method, inference and communication.
- Decide whether a request needs description, an experiment, a causal analysis, a predictive model or no analysis.

# DS-311 · Data Quality, Labelling and Pipelines for Analysis

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-300.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)

Participants build the data an analysis depends on for Bayyin Consumer Protection Office, a fictional regulator holding 30,000 synthetic complaint records in Arabic and English. - Implement quality rules with thresholds and severities, and a data contract for the prepared table.
- Build a reproducible preparation pipeline from raw extracts to an analysis-ready table that stops on a blocking rule.
- Diagnose why an analytical figure changed after a data refresh and decide on the correction.

# DS-401 · Bayesian Modelling and Decisions under Uncertainty

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-401/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-401/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-401/practice.html

## Description

Participants build Bayesian models that support decisions and judge models built by others. On synthetic burst records from 140 districts of a fictional water utility, they test priors by simulation, fit and diagnose Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, pool small districts hierarchically, check and compare models by predictive accuracy, and verify code by simulation-based calibration. The last day turns posteriors into a replacement plan by expected utility and prices a proposed leak survey by its value of information.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement a Bayesian workflow from prior predictive simulation to sampler diagnosis.
- Design a hierarchical model for districts with very unequal data and defend the pooling it implies.
- Evaluate competing models by posterior predictive checks and approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and choose one for the decision.
- Diagnose an error in a model implementation by parameter recovery and simulation-based calibration.
- Decide a replacement plan by expected utility under the posterior and price further data by its value of information.
- Review another analyst's Bayesian analysis for priors, computation, checking and reporting.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-301.md)
- Fits and interprets generalised linear models in code
- Simulates from probability distributions and computes a likelihood

## Format and days

### Day 1: From priors to posteriors

- Models that generate data
- Priors you can defend
- Fitting with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
- Reading the computation

### Day 2: Pooling across districts

- No, complete and partial pooling
- Group-level predictors
- The funnel and non-centred models
- Under-reporting as measurement error

### Day 3: Is the model good enough

- Posterior predictive checks
- Comparing models by predictive accuracy
- Is the code right
- How much the priors matter

### Day 4: From posterior to decision

- Loss, utility and the decision table
- Choosing under a budget
- What more data is worth
- Reviewing a Bayesian analysis

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Priors and computation

- Generative models and weakly informative priors
- Prior predictive simulation
- Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, diagnostics and reparameterisation
- When approximate inference suffices

### Hierarchical models

- Partial pooling and shrinkage
- Group-level predictors
- Under-reporting as measurement error

### Checking and comparing

- Posterior predictive checks
- Approximate leave-one-out cross-validation
- Simulation-based calibration
- Prior sensitivity

### Decisions

- Expected utility over posterior draws
- Value of information
- Expected loss explained to risk owners

---

# DS-403 · Statistical Evaluation of AI Systems

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-403/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-403/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-403/practice.html

## Description

Participants treat every evaluation of an AI system as an experiment with a sampling design. On item-level results from small open-weight models on a fictional permits authority's synthetic bilingual task set, they compute clustered standard errors, compare systems with paired designs, size evaluations within a budget, use exact or Bayesian intervals for small sets, correct for grader error and audit benchmark claims. Graders and harnesses are built in AE-303, not here.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute standard errors and intervals for an evaluation score that account for clustered items, repeated samples and small item counts.
- Decide whether the difference between two systems is real and large enough to matter, using a paired analysis.
- Design an evaluation's size in items, samples per item and grader calls to detect a stated difference within budget.
- Evaluate the bias that grader error adds to a pass rate and correct it, carrying calibration uncertainty into the interval.
- Audit an evaluation claim for statistical validity, contamination risk and unequal tuning or token budgets.
- Design a reporting standard for evaluation claims, including results by language and subgroup.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-302 · Online Experiments and A/B Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-302.md)
- [DS-305 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-305.md)
- Computes bootstrap intervals and paired tests in code
- Has logged a language model's outputs through an API

## Format and days

### Day 1: Scores have standard errors

- An evaluation is a sample
- Clustered items
- Repeated samples
- Plan before results

### Day 2: Comparing systems

- Paired designs
- Many configurations
- Sizing an evaluation
- Spending the budget

### Day 3: Small sets and imperfect graders

- Where large-sample intervals fail
- Exact and Bayesian intervals
- Graders against people
- Correcting for grader error

### Day 4: Auditing claims and setting standards

- Contamination and unequal budgets
- Auditing a report
- Slicing by language
- A reporting standard

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Evaluations as experiments

- Items as a sample from a task population
- Variance from items, samples and graders
- Pass rates over repeated attempts
- Pre-registered analysis plans

### Comparisons and sizing

- Clustered standard errors and design effects
- Paired differences and multiple comparisons
- Sizing by formula and simulation

### Small sets and graders

- Exact and Bayesian intervals
- Correcting pass rates for grader error

### Claims and standards

- Contamination, unequal budgets and saturation
- Reporting by language and subgroup

---

# DS-404 · Advanced Modelling for Structured Data

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-404/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-404/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-404/practice.html

## Description

Participants decide when pretrained models, ensembles and decision-aware pipelines earn their place in structured-data work. On a fictional food wholesaler's synthetic orders and demand, they test pretrained tabular models and zero-shot forecasters against tuned baselines, stack ensembles, turn forecasts into orders by optimisation, score models by decision cost and validate under the shift of a new depot region. They end with an adoption decision weighing accuracy, licence, cost and data residency.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Evaluate a pretrained tabular model against a tuned, ensembled boosted-tree baseline across training-set sizes.
- Evaluate zero-shot pretrained forecasters, with and without covariates, against statistical and tuned learned benchmarks by rolling-origin backtests.
- Implement a stacked ensemble from out-of-fold or rolling-origin predictions and measure its improvement over the best single model.
- Build a predict-then-optimise pipeline and judge forecasters by the decision cost they cause.
- Diagnose distribution shift between training and deployment data and validate a model under it.
- Decide whether to adopt a pretrained model for one task, weighing accuracy, cost, licence and data residency.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-304 · Forecasting and Time Series](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-304.md)
- [DS-305 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-305.md)
- Tunes boosted-tree models with cross-validation
- Backtests forecasters with rolling-origin cross-validation
- Formulates a simple linear programme, or completes the pre-work

## Format and days

### Day 1: Pretrained models for tables

- Tuned boosted trees first
- In-context learning on tables
- Learning curves decide
- Reading a leaderboard claim

### Day 2: Forecasting with pretrained models

- Zero-shot against a benchmark floor
- Where zero-shot loses
- Holidays that move
- Ensembles worth their cost

### Day 3: From forecast to order

- Asymmetric costs
- Optimising under capacity
- Scoring by regret
- Uncertainty in the plan

### Day 4: Shift and adoption

- Detecting shift
- Validating under shift
- Correcting for shift
- Adoption conditions

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Pretrained models for tables and time series

- In-context learning on tables and its size limits
- Zero-shot forecasting with covariates
- Intermittent and short series
- Leaderboard claims and tuning budgets

### Ensembling and decisions

- Out-of-fold and rolling-origin stacking
- Newsvendor logic
- Integer programmes for orders
- Decision regret

### Validation under shift

- Covariate, label and concept shift
- Adversarial, grouped and temporal validation
- Weighted conformal intervals

### Adoption conditions

- Licences and permitted use
- Data residency and classification
- Subgroup error after shift

# DS-405 · Data Preparation at Scale: Contracts, Synthetic Data and Privacy

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-405/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-405/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-405/practice.html

## Description

Participants run data preparation for the fictional Rimah Health Data Consortium: three hospital groups send encounter, laboratory and pharmacy extracts (about 30 million synthetic rows) for a readmission study, and a university partner wants a copy. They contract and link the producers, rebuild preparation as an incremental pipeline over partitioned columnar tables, generate and attack synthetic versions, compare privacy-enhancing methods for four requests, and write a release decision a privacy officer could sign. Single-table contracts come from DS-311; de-identification and basic differential privacy from DS-309.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design shared data contracts, a pseudonymous linkage key and a breaking-change policy for a feed with several producers.
- Implement an incremental, idempotent preparation pipeline over partitioned columnar tables with quality gates.
- Evaluate a synthetic dataset for fidelity, analytical utility and disclosure risk.
- Compute differentially private statistics under a budget shared across repeated releases.
- Select a privacy-enhancing method for each data request by comparing protection, utility and cost.
- Decide whether to release a dataset and on what conditions, and defend the decision.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-309 · Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-309.md)
- Writes SQL with window functions and cleans data with a data-frame library
- Has written a data contract and blocking quality rules for one table (DS-311 or equivalent)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Contract the producers

- Preparation breaks where producers disagree
- One contract, three producers
- Linking patients across producers
- Versions and breaking changes

### Day 2: Prepare at scale

- Columnar files and lazy execution
- Incremental and idempotent loads
- Tables with history
- Gates and lineage at scale

### Day 3: Synthesise and attack

- When synthetic data fits
- Generating related tables
- Utility is measured against the analysis
- Privacy is measured by attack

### Day 4: Protect and decide

- Disclosure risk in longitudinal records
- Privacy budgets over many releases
- Analysis without pooling records
- The release decision

### Day 5: Capstone: a release package and its defence


## Topics

### Contracts across producers

- Producer and consumer duties
- Code and unit harmonisation as contract clauses
- Keyed pseudonyms for record linkage
- Versions, deprecation and breaking changes

### Pipelines for large data

- Lazy columnar execution and partitions
- Idempotent, incremental loads
- Snapshots in open table formats
- Quality gates and lineage events

### Synthetic data

- What it is for and what it cannot do
- Relational generators
- Fidelity and fitness for the analysis
- Distance and membership-inference tests

### Privacy-enhancing methods and release

- Disclosure risk in longitudinal and linked records
- Privacy budgets across releases
- Federated analysis, secure aggregation and clean rooms
- Lawful basis, secondary use and release conditions

# DS-406 · Measuring the Impact of Data and AI Programmes

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-406/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-406/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-406/practice.html

## Description

Participants evaluate three programmes of the fictional Al-Rawdah Municipal Services Authority: a drafting assistant rolled out in phases to 24 permit offices, a citizen service chatbot and a data-sharing platform. They turn claims into outcome measures, design a trial for a rollout still to come, estimate the effect of one that has happened while correcting for the keenest offices adopting first, carry the uncertainty into a value case, and brief a panel playing the executive committee on whether to stop, continue or scale. DS-302 and DS-303 teach the methods; this course applies them to programmes.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare an outcome framework that separates activity, speed, quality and value and links each measure to a programme claim.
- Design an evaluation for a programme before rollout, choosing among randomised, stepped-wedge and encouragement designs and setting unit, duration and power.
- Estimate the effect of a completed rollout while correcting for selection into adoption, and test the result's sensitivity.
- Build a value case that carries the effect's uncertainty through costs, benefits and break-even.
- Evaluate an impact report from a vendor or internal team and decide whether it supports scaling.
- Present programme impact to leadership with uncertainty in plain words and one clear recommendation.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-302 · Online Experiments and A/B Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-302.md)
- [DS-303 · Causal Inference from Observational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-303.md)
- Estimates a difference-in-differences model and reads an event-study plot
- Runs a power calculation by simulation

## Format and days

### Day 1: What would show it worked

- Claims, logic models and estimands
- Outcomes that matter
- Measuring quality by blind review
- Perceived versus measured gains

### Day 2: Design before the rollout

- Units, clusters and design effects
- Stepped-wedge rollouts
- When use cannot be forced
- The measurement plan

### Day 3: After the rollout

- Selection into adoption
- The phased rollout as evidence
- Who gains and who loses
- Effects that spill or fade

### Day 4: From estimate to decision

- Value with uncertainty
- A programme view for leadership
- Reviewing an impact report
- Stop, continue or scale

### Day 5: Capstone: the impact briefing


## Topics

### What programmes claim

- Logic models and estimands
- Activity, speed, quality and value
- Blind review of sampled work
- Perceived versus measured gains

### Designs before rollout

- Cluster randomisation and design effects
- Stepped-wedge and encouragement designs
- Measurement plans fixed in advance

### After the rollout

- Selection into adoption
- Staggered rollouts as natural experiments
- Who gains and who loses
- Spillover, novelty and fading effects

### From estimate to decision

- Value cases as distributions
- Programme views for leadership
- Stop, continue or scale

# DS-407 · Leading Analytical Work: Review, Standards and Stakeholders

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Data Science: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DS-400.md)
- On the learning path: [Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/index.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-407/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-407/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ds-407/practice.html

## Description

Participants lead the analytics unit of the fictional Ras Sahil Ports Authority: twelve analysts whose work increasingly starts as an assistant's draft. They write a proportionate quality-assurance standard and review checklist, re-run and review colleagues' analyses, set the unit's rules for AI-assisted work, turn review findings into feedback, and negotiate scope, deadline and evidence with role-played sponsors, one of whom asks for an unfavourable result to be dropped. DS-310 teaches reviewing one analysis; this course sets the standards and runs the system.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design a proportionate quality-assurance standard for analytical work, with assurance levels, a review checklist and sign-off rules.
- Review analyses by others, including assistant-drafted ones, rank findings by their effect on the decision and calibrate severity with a second reviewer.
- Design rules for AI-assisted analysis covering verification, disclosure and the process evidence each analyst keeps, and audit the unit's work against them.
- Prepare feedback and a development plan for an analyst from review findings.
- Lead a negotiation with a sponsor on scope, deadline and evidence threshold and record the agreement.
- Decide how to respond to pressure to change or suppress a finding, and record the reasons.

## Prerequisites

- [DS-310 · Problem Framing and Analytical Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DS-310.md)
- Has reviewed an analysis written by someone else and written comments the author acted on
- Uses version control for analysis code

## Format and days

### Day 1: Set the standard

- Assurance proportionate to risk
- A team review checklist
- Reproducibility as a team rule
- Rules for AI-assisted analysis

### Day 2: Review and develop

- Calibrating reviewers
- Auditing assisted work
- Feedback that builds skill
- Review capacity and mentoring

### Day 3: Work with sponsors

- Scope and deadline
- Agreeing the evidence first
- Pressure on a finding
- Reporting quality and correcting errors

### Day 4: Capstone: the staffing pack and the review meeting


## Topics

### Analytical quality assurance

- Assurance proportionate to risk and use
- Analyst, reviewer and approver roles
- Published guides such as the Aqua Book and the REFORMS checklist
- Correcting errors found after release

### Review practice

- Question fit, data, method, inference, communication
- Re-running before reading
- Severity by effect on the decision
- Calibrating reviewers

### AI-assisted work and developing analysts

- Verification and disclosure rules
- Auditing assisted work against the rules
- Feedback that names the reasoning
- Keeping unaided practice in the work

### Sponsors and evidence

- Scope, deadline and answerability
- Agreeing the evidence that would change the decision
- Pressure on findings and escalation
- Quality statements in board papers
